findings.title: Production Postgres credential hardcoded in a tracked script
findings.evidence: scripts/run_schema_migration_prod.py deleted; tests/test_migration_tooling.py::test_sec01_leaking_script_is_deleted_and_never_returns; no DSN literal remains in scripts/. ROTATION PLANNING this session: coordinated real, read-only reconnaissance with the AWS-equipped sibling session (nothing written/rotated/redeployed) to sequence the rotation safely. Findings: (1) the real secret is `vyomquant/production/database_url` (arn:aws:secretsmanager:ap-southeast-1:273709947018:secret:vyomquant/production/database_url-s7iUfF), manual rotation only (Supabase-hosted Postgres has no native AWS rotation Lambda integration), already has AWSCURRENT+AWSPREVIOUS versions so it has been updated via put-secret-value before. (2) Exactly one consumer account-wide: the vyomquant-api container of task definition vyomquant-api:214, under the single ECS service vyomquant-api-service-cjema2sl in vyomquant-cluster -- reconfirmed no worker services exist in production at all (same finding as INF-03/OPS-TRAIN-01), so nothing else needs coordinating. (3) ECS resolves secrets/valueFrom only at task LAUNCH time, never live-reloaded into a running container -- updating the secret's value alone does nothing until a force-new-deployment (same task definition revision 214, no new revision needed) launches fresh tasks that re-resolve it. (4) The service's deployment config is ROLLING (minimumHealthyPercent=100/maximumPercent=200) with the deployment circuit breaker enabled (rollback: true) -- a force-new-deployment launches a second task and waits for it to pass the ALB health check before stopping the old one, so it never goes through zero running tasks, AND if the new task's DATABASE_URL were to point at a password Supabase hasn't been updated to yet, the new task fails its readiness check and ECS automatically rolls back on its own with the old task still healthy -- no manual rollback needed for that ordering mistake. The real risk direction is the OPPOSITE order: if Supabase's password changes BEFORE the AWS secret is updated and redeployed, the currently-running task's existing pooled connections likely survive (Postgres doesn't kill live sessions on a password change, only new connection attempts need the new password) but new connection attempts from that stale task would start failing immediately -- a general Postgres fact, not independently verified against this app's specific pool/reconnect behavior. Correct sequence per this evidence: stage the new value in Secrets Manager -> flip the password in Supabase -> force-new-deployment, as close together as practical. INCIDENT, 2026-10-23 -- SEC-01 IS MATERIALLY WORSE THAN FILED AND THE REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC. This finding was scoped to one file (scripts/run_schema_migration_prod.py) and its remaining work recorded as 'rotate the password'. Scoped to that file the evidence said the exposure was ALREADY CLOSED, and that sub-conclusion is correct: the password in that file is 23 chars, the live one is 17, both name the same role (postgres.wrkexcjqnidkdrayhlsi on aws-1-ap-southeast-1.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres, verified), PostgreSQL stores one password per role, and the live DSN was proven to authenticate (`--verify` connected as postgres at 2026-10-23T08:26:13Z). So that file's leaked value is dead. THAT CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE FILE AND WRONG ABOUT THE REPOSITORY. A full-history sweep of all 20 readable production Secrets Manager values against `git log --all -p` (481,799,695 chars) matched THREE OTHER LIVE SECRETS, in files this finding never named: (1) vyomquant/production/master_encryption_keys, WHOLE VALUE, in `aws_secrets_deploy.py`, first published 2026-07-22 (4428a4daaa) -- ~93 days public; this is the MultiFernet key protecting exchange_keys.encrypted_api_key/encrypted_secret_key/encrypted_password (2 rows live). (2) vyomquant/production/jwt_secret, WHOLE VALUE, same file and date; HMAC key for platform-minted tokens such as strategy_operations.py:5704's model-download token. (3) vyomquant/production/database_url PASSWORD COMPONENT, across 15 files under scripts/, first published 2026-08-14 (12a799e603), commits 12a799e603/8992f2eda7/659c04df77/fbaf266fdb -- the last of which is titled 'Remediate SEC-01, ...', i.e. the remediation commit MOVED the literal instead of removing it from history. All three are absent from HEAD and present in history, so a working-tree scan cannot see them and `git clone` recovers all three. gh repo view: visibility=PUBLIC, forks=0, collaborators=1, deploy keys=0. NOT AN INCIDENT, recorded so it is not conflated: supabase_anon_key also matched, but Supabase anon keys are PUBLIC BY DESIGN (shipped in the browser bundle, stored as the VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY CI secret for that purpose, protected by RLS not secrecy). SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET IS CLEAN -- user logins are Supabase-issued and verified with that secret, so existing sessions are NOT forgeable from what leaked. COVERAGE CAVEAT: 20/21 secrets compared; vyomquant/production/supabase_key returned ResourceNotFound and is UNKNOWN, not clean. METHOD CORRECTION worth recording: the FIRST sweep reported 'live values loaded for comparison: 4' against 11 watched secrets and still printed a verdict -- Secrets Manager throttles rapid get-secret-value calls and the loader treated a non-zero exit as a silent skip, so 7 secrets were unchecked while the output looked complete. The replacement (sec01_full_sweep.py) retries with backoff, fails loudly on an unreadable secret, and reports per-secret OUTCOME so 'clean' is distinguishable from 'not checked'. ROTATION MECHANICS VERIFIED BEFORE RECOMMENDING: MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEYS rotation is NON-DESTRUCTIVE because api_key_vault.py:96-99 builds a MultiFernet from a comma-separated list (first encrypts, all decrypt) and already ships generate_new_master_key() + rotate_key(); but core/credential_vault.py:285 takes ONLY the first key through PBKDF2 to derive a single Fernet, so prepending there would silently orphan its ciphertext -- it has NO production callers (its own module, tests, and test_strategy_dag_architecture.py which treats importing it as a violation) and stores to Redis not Postgres, so it carries no data today, but it is a live trap for any future rotation. Full write-up: docs/launch_readiness/SEC-01_INCIDENT.md SEVERITY CORRECTION, same day, for the master_encryption_keys component of this finding: it exposes NO customer credential. Filed VAULT-01 separately. Every one of the 4 ciphertext values in exchange_keys was tested against all 265 structurally valid Fernet keys recoverable from the full git history, and none decrypt -- the rows were encrypted 2026-06-21 under a key that exists in neither Secrets Manager nor git. So an attacker holding the leaked master key can decrypt nothing that is currently stored. It must STILL be rotated, because it is the key that would encrypt every FUTURE credential and it is public -- but the exposure is prospective, not retrospective, and calling it CRITICAL alongside the database password overstated it. The database password was the genuinely critical one and is now ROTATED AND VERIFIED: scripts/audit_secrets_in_git_history.py reports vyomquant/production/database_url as clean, a new AWSCURRENT version was created 2026-10-23T15:26:16+05:30 with the prior value retained as AWSPREVIOUS, the service rolled 232->234 and reports COMPLETED with running=1/1 HEALTHY, and the stored DSN connects as postgres. jwt_secret remains exposed and unrotated; scripts/rotate_jwt_secret.py is built and its --plan confirms the current value IS in history. ALL THREE ROTATIONS COMPLETE AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, 2026-10-23. scripts/audit_secrets_in_git_history.py now prints 'NO LIVE SECRET IS RECOVERABLE FROM GIT HISTORY' and exits 0. Per secret: (1) database_url -- rotated via scripts/rotate_database_password.py, new AWSCURRENT at 2026-10-23T15:26:16+05:30 with the prior value retained as AWSPREVIOUS, service rolled 232->234, reports clean. (2) jwt_secret -- rotated via scripts/rotate_jwt_secret.py, fingerprint 1ba08925c720 -> 69ec7601df82, version 1761003f-0031-48ec-b1da-bea0f6acea38, deployment COMPLETED, --verify confirms production-grade AND absent from history. The value was generated in-process and never printed, prompted for, pasted, or placed on a command line, so no human ever handled it -- strictly less exposure than the database rotation, which needed an operator to carry the value to the Supabase dashboard. (3) master_encryption_keys -- rotated via scripts/rotate_master_encryption_keys.py, fingerprint baff8a448794 -> bade92adbfb2 by prepend, redeploy, then retire of the old key (a second redeploy followed), ending at a single key; --verify confirms 1 key present and NOT in history. PRODUCTION HEALTH AFTER THREE CONSECUTIVE DEPLOYMENTS: ECS task RUNNING health=HEALTHY, running=1/1, rolloutState=COMPLETED on vyomquant-api:234, ALB target group state 'healthy', and the stored DSN connects as postgres. None of the three deployments failed or rolled back. The jwt_secret rotation is additionally proven by the boot itself: main.py:320 calls assert_jwt_secret_is_production_grade() and raises on a weak value, so a task that reaches RUNNING has necessarily accepted the new secret. WHAT REMAINS FOR SEC-01, AND IT IS NO LONGER A LIVE EXPOSURE: (a) two ORPHANED secrets, /vyomquant/production/MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEYS and /vyomquant/production/JWT_SECRET, still hold the OLD published values. They are referenced by NOTHING -- confirmed against the running task definition's 11 valueFrom ARNs -- so what they contain authenticates nothing now that the secrets ECS actually reads have been rotated. Secret sprawl holding dead material; remedy is DELETE, not rotate. (b) the git-history purge of all the old literals, still a destructive action awaiting explicit instruction. (c) vyomquant/production/supabase_key returns ResourceNotFound, so sweep coverage is 20/21 and that one is UNKNOWN rather than clean. (d) repository visibility is still PUBLIC. TOOL CORRECTION made in the same pass: the sweep was reporting supabase_anon_key as an exposure and, after the rotations, the two orphans as 'LIVE SECRET(S) ... must be rotated'. Both were wrong in a way that matters -- an alert carrying known-benign entries teaches its reader to skim past the real ones. It now reads the running task definition to classify LIVE vs ORPHANED, treats Supabase anon keys as public by design (they ship in the browser bundle; safety rests on RLS, not secrecy), and exits non-zero ONLY for a live exposure so a scheduled run stays meaningful.
findings.verification_level: code; rotation sequence fully planned and verified against real AWS state (read-only) this session, not yet executed
findings.remaining_action: NO LIVE EXPOSURE REMAINS. All three leaked secrets are rotated and the sweep exits 0. Four residuals, none of them a live credential: (1) DELETE the orphaned uppercase secrets /vyomquant/production/MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEYS and /vyomquant/production/JWT_SECRET, which hold the old published values and are read by nothing. `aws secretsmanager delete-secret` keeps a 7-30 day recovery window, so this is reversible. Consider the other four unreferenced uppercase duplicates too (DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY): the last three currently MIRROR live values, which is worse than holding dead ones, because a rotation will silently leave them stale and a future operator may wire one up. (2) THE GIT-HISTORY PURGE (git filter-repo + force-push) of every old literal. Destructive, rewrites published history, needs explicit instruction, and does not reach existing clones -- which is exactly why rotation was the control that mattered and why this is now hygiene rather than incident response. (3) RESOLVE vyomquant/production/supabase_key (ResourceNotFound) so sweep coverage is 21/21 rather than 20/21 with one UNKNOWN. (4) REPOSITORY IS STILL PUBLIC. Making it private bounds the exposure of anything not yet found, and nothing found so far suggests the sweep has seen everything -- it only compares against secrets that exist in Secrets Manager today, so a credential that was leaked and then deleted from AWS would not be detected by it at all. ALSO: schedule scripts/audit_secrets_in_git_history.py. The defect class was never one careless file; it was that nothing watched for this.

findings.title: Any signed-in user can grant themselves a paid plan, raise limits and unfreeze their account via Supabase REST
findings.evidence: exploit reproduced then blocked on real Postgres; tests/test_sec07_profiles_platform_columns_postgres.py (13) VERIFICATION STRENGTHENED (this session, no code change): this finding's regression file, tests/test_sec07_profiles_platform_columns_postgres.py, was named in NO PostgreSQL lane in 01-pr-check.yml, so its assertions skipped in the SQLite lane and ran against a real server nowhere -- including in run 39695784610, where all 8 jobs were green. The evidence above ('exploit reproduced then blocked on real Postgres') was therefore true of a prior local session and had never been re-established by this repository's own pipeline. CI-11 (opened this session) wires the file into the provisioning lane, and it now passes there against real PostgreSQL 17: run 39728990457, job 119660118669 shows test_user_cannot_change_platform_columns_on_own_row PASSED for every escalation vector this finding named -- subscription_tier='enterprise', max_api_slots=99, is_frozen=false, balance=1000000, plan_limit_overrides, available_discounts, billing_currency='INR', referred_by_user_id -- plus test_user_cannot_modify_another_users_row and test_browser_roles_cannot_insert_or_delete_profiles. The P0's fix is now proven by the pipeline, not only by a session transcript. *** CRITICAL CORRECTION (Kiro, 2026-10-22): THIS P0 WAS STILL LIVE-EXPLOITABLE IN PRODUCTION while recorded VERIFIED_FIXED, and has now been closed there. *** Checked the real production database directly for the first time. `anon` AND `authenticated` both held DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE on public.profiles -- table-level, so every column was writable, including all six platform-owned ones that exist there (subscription_tier, max_api_slots, is_frozen, balance, available_discounts, billing_currency). RLS was enabled but NOT forced, and its 'Update own profile' policy constrains WHICH ROW, not WHICH COLUMNS -- so a signed-in user updating their own row could set their own plan, raise their own API slots, clear their own freeze and write their own balance through the REST API with their own JWT. Exactly this finding's described exploit, unmitigated. ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISRECORD: migration 033 was written and tested but never applied to production -- `recorded_migrations` does not exist in that database at all -- and this entry's own remaining_action said so ('Apply migration 033 to staging/production (human-run)') while the status read VERIFIED_FIXED. Earlier the same day this entry's evidence was strengthened because its regression tests now pass in CI; they pass against a database provisioned from REPOSITORY SOURCE, which says nothing about the deployed one. That scope limit was stated at the time and this is what it cost. REMEDIATION APPLIED: one transaction, verified before commit, revoking INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER from anon and authenticated; SELECT deliberately retained because RLS scopes reads to the caller's own row and the profile page depends on it; service_role and postgres untouched. Safe because the frontend never writes profiles through Supabase REST -- grepped every .js/.jsx under algo22-terminal/src for `.from('profiles')` (no matches) and for `profiles` generally (comments, docstrings and reads via the backend's own GET /api/user/profile only). Verified after: anon and authenticated hold SELECT only; UPDATE on every sensitive column reads False; ECS service healthy at 1/1 running, 0 pending. EXPOSURE ASSESSED, NOT ASSUMED: all 182 profiles are still subscription_tier='free', with 0 paid tiers, 0 max_api_slots>1, 0 available_discounts, 0 next_billing_date, 0 payment_provider, and every payment table empty (billing_invoices, invoices, payment_methods, subscriptions all 0 rows). The only non-zero values were 7 `balance` rows sharing one identical microsecond timestamp (2026-08-14 03:12:57.680311+00) -- a single batch seed, six of them exactly 1000.0 and one an obvious dev artifact. CONCLUSION: the hole was open but NOT exploited, because the platform is pre-launch with no paying users. Had it launched with that grant in place, the first user to read the anon key out of the JS bundle could have granted themselves Enterprise. *** SECOND CORRECTION (Kiro, 2026-10-22, same session): THE FIX I APPLIED EARLIER TODAY OVERSHOT AND BROKE THREE USER-FACING FEATURES IN PRODUCTION. Now repaired. *** My earlier production fix revoked INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES and TRIGGER on public.profiles from anon and authenticated. Migration 033 -- the fix actually designed for this finding -- revokes only INSERT and DELETE, and column-scopes UPDATE with a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger (guard_profiles_platform_columns) that rejects any change outside an allowlist of username, display_name, avatar_url, bio, telegram_id, full_name, preferred_currency, updated_at. It keeps UPDATE deliberately, because three user-facing writes reach profiles as the `authenticated` role -- they use a Supabase client built from the ANON key carrying the end user's JWT (core/dependencies.py: create_request_supabase:148, create_request_supabase_async:242, and the get_request_supabase dependency at :389): routers/user.py:93 update_profile, core/pricing_service.py:324 set_user_currency_preference, backend/account_lifecycle.py:215 delete_account. MEASURED, not inferred: with table-wide UPDATE revoked, all three failed in production with 'permission denied for table profiles'. So the escalation was closed and profile editing, currency preference and account deletion were all broken at the same time. REPAIRED in one verified transaction: installed migration 033's trigger function and trigger, then GRANT UPDATE ON public.profiles TO authenticated (anon deliberately NOT restored -- no path-(A) write is ever the anon role). INSERT, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES and TRIGGER remain revoked from both browser roles. Re-verified on a fresh connection afterwards: authenticated CAN update full_name and preferred_currency (1 row each); authenticated CANNOT set subscription_tier, flip is_frozen, set balance, or DELETE a profile row -- each refused with 'platform-controlled columns cannot be modified by role authenticated' (SQLSTATE 42501). ECS service healthy throughout (task vyomquant-api:224, 1/1 RUNNING, healthStatus HEALTHY, rolloutState COMPLETED). ONE RESIDUAL, FIXED IN CODE: delete_account writes `email` and `is_frozen`, which are correctly NOT in the allowlist -- a role that can SET is_frozen can also CLEAR it, which is precisely this finding's 'unfreeze their account' vector, so an account cannot be frozen with the credentials of the account being frozen. account_lifecycle.delete_account now takes an optional service_supabase and uses it for step 4 only, while steps 1-3 keep the user-scoped client because RLS is what confines them to the caller's own rows; routers/user.py resolves it via get_service_supabase_async(). Pinned by tests/test_priv01_account_export_and_deletion.py::test_the_profile_anonymisation_uses_the_service_client_not_the_users and ::test_delete_account_still_works_when_no_service_client_is_supplied (11/11 passing, was 9). NOTE on the trigger's semantics, verified deliberately: it compares to_jsonb(NEW) - allowlist against to_jsonb(OLD) - allowlist, i.e. VALUES not column lists, so writing a platform column to the value it already holds is permitted. A first verification run asserted 'SET is_frozen = false' must be refused and failed the assertion -- the profile was already unfrozen, making the write a no-op. The change set correctly rolled itself back on that failed assertion; the test was corrected to flip the value (SET is_frozen = NOT is_frozen) and then passed.
findings.verification_level: production (escalation re-attempted and refused on a fresh connection AFTER the repair; the three path-(A) writes re-attempted and two confirmed working, the third intentionally blocked and fixed in code with tests) + code+test
findings.remaining_action: Migration 033 is now applied to production as a trigger, but production still has no migration ledger (see DEPLOY-05), so nothing in the database records that. Reconcile when recorded_migrations is created.

findings.title: Paper Sessions (the persisted, canonical paper-trading path) can never start
findings.evidence: Built the missing persistence layer for the measurement that Requirement 14.4's correctness floor (already real) was never given anywhere to read: backend_app/backend/market_data_measurement_store.py (record_measurement, latest_measurements, MeasurementStoreUnavailable; service-role only) + migration 039_market_data_source_measurements.sql (append-only, RLS enabled, no browser-role policy, explicit REVOKE/GRANT). market_data_latency.py gained from_dict on LatencySummary and SourceMeasurement (exact inverses of to_dict, explicitly skipping derived properties) so a stored row round-trips byte-for-byte. routers/paper_trading.py's _recorded_measurements() now reads the store instead of hardcoded None. scripts/record_market_data_measurement.py is the operator CLI that runs the existing tests/perf/test_market_data_latency.py::run_experiment() and persists whatever it actually measured (never an invented/unmeasured result). tests/test_rt04_measurement_store_round_trips.py (6 tests, fake-Supabase double): round-trip fidelity, newest-row-wins per source, unknown source refused before any write, no-rows-yet is an empty dict not a fabricated pair, an unreadable store raises rather than reading as silently unmeasured. tests/test_task_28_1_session_routes.py updated for the new async seam. Full regression this session: targeted RT-04/RT-16/RT-21 suite (45 passed/1 skipped) + a broader paper/market_data pass (1676 passed, 50 skipped, 0 failed) + full validation_sweep/schema_drift/session_routes (584 passed, 2 failed -- confirmed pre-existing, unrelated billing-route findings present on the clean tree before this change). Commit 838a0ed. *** RT-04's BLOCKER IS NOT WALL-CLOCK TIME (Kiro, 2026-10-23). *** This was recorded as EXTERNAL_BLOCKED pending 'roughly a week of continuous measurement against the real production feed with real outbound network access'. Both halves of that turned out to be wrong, and the real blocker is a platform defect now recorded as DATA-03. FIRST, the network access was available. Candidate B's probe needs only TCP reachability to the venue (`probe_candidate_b` -> api.binance.com:443) -- NOT Redis and NOT the MDS process, which only Candidate A requires. Verified from this machine: the venue is reachable, CCXT connected and loaded 4,697 markets, and a direct klines fetch returns bars. So the measurement did not need INF-03's workers at all, and could have been started at any point. SECOND, the operator tool had NEVER WORKED. `scripts/record_market_data_measurement.py` ran `asyncio.run(_main(...))` and called the synchronous `run_experiment()` from inside it -- but `run_experiment` drives its own coroutines with `asyncio.run()` internally (`observe_ingest_processing_cost`, tests/perf/test_market_data_latency.py:616, and `_measure_candidate_b`'s poll loop), and asyncio refuses to start a loop inside a running one: 'RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop'. The script therefore raised before reaching the persistence step and had never recorded a measurement. On the prescribed window that failure would have surfaced at the END of a multi-day run with nothing persisted. Found by running a 60-second window first; fixed structurally -- the experiment now runs at top level with no loop running, and only the genuinely async persistence gets its own asyncio.run. ALSO FIXED: `--resolve-config-from-aws` reads SUPABASE_URL/EXCHANGE_ID from the deployed vyomquant-api task definition and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/REDIS_URL from Secrets Manager, printing names only and never values. Persisting a measurement needs the service-role credential, and requiring an operator to hand-export four values correctly first was part of why this had not been run. It warns before a long window if the persistence credentials are still missing, rather than letting the run discover it at the end. THIRD, AND THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: with the tool fixed and the venue reachable, the run still produced NOT_MEASURED -- because the platform's OWN validator refused real exchange data: 'DATA_QUALITY: ... Found 1 outliers in close log-returns using z_score for UNKNOWN. Dataset rejected'. Measured against 12,000 live BTC/USDT 1m bars, 100% of 10,000-bar windows are rejected at every threshold from 3.0 to 10.0 because the whole window is refused on any single exceedance. See DATA-03. Running the prescribed window would not have closed this finding; it would have burned a week and produced the same NOT_MEASURED. ||| CLOSED (Kiro). A MEASUREMENT NOW EXISTS, PASSES THE FLOOR, AND IS PERSISTED IN PRODUCTION. This entry recorded 'No measurement has ever produced a result'; that was confirmed empirically first -- a read-only query of production found market_data_source_measurements present (migration 039 applied) with ZERO rows. STEP 1, DATA-03 resolved (see that entry). STEP 2, the prescribed 60s smoke run, which is what this entry asked for next: Candidate B went from NOT_MEASURED with 'DATA_QUALITY: Found 1 outliers in close log-returns ... Dataset rejected' to delivering validated windows -- 'Validation complete for BTC/USDT 1m: score=95.0, issues=1', repeatedly -- with measured=True and completeness=1.0. So DATA-03 was the whole of the blocker this entry named. THE 'THEN 7 DAYS WALL-CLOCK' WAS AN ARTEFACT OF THE HARNESS, NOT THE REQUIREMENT, and that is the finding that let this close today. The smoke run returned expected_bars=999 against a floor of >=10,000, so completeness_sample could never pass. The cause: _measure_candidate_b called `fetch_historical_ohlcv(..., limit=1000)` -- a HARDCODED 1,000 against a floor requiring DEFAULT_FLOOR.min_completeness_sample_bars = 10,000 (itself derived from 1/(1-0.9999)). Completeness here is computed from the BAR TIMESTAMPS ('a closed 1m bar is due every 60s between the oldest and the newest bar delivered'), so with a 1,000-bar request the delivered grid saturated at ~999 whatever the window length, and only NEW bars closing during the run could widen it -- ~9,000 more minutes, which is precisely the 'roughly seven days of continuous measurement' this entry and migration 039 both record. The venue serves that grid in one paginated read. FIXED by deriving the depth from the floor instead of hardcoding it -- the same 'read it, do not restate it' pattern test_paper_market_feed_selection.py already uses for the same constant. `fetch_historical_ohlcv`'s default mode pages BACKWARD since DATA-01 ('it now pages backward: after the latest page, each request starts one page-width before the oldest bar held'), so a deeper limit is honoured rather than silently truncated at one page -- which is the defect DATA-01 fixed. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT CLAIM IS UNCHANGED. Candidate B's live ARRIVAL half still needs Redis, and end-to-end/ingest latency remain None because a historical bar's age is not its delivery time -- the harness's own existing reasoning, untouched. What is measured is exactly what the floor checks: completeness over the grid, ordering, duplicates, invalid OHLC, synthetic candles, plus the pipeline latency an executor actually waits for. RESULT, all six floor checks passed: measured=True, expected_bars=10,003 (>=10,000), completeness=1.0 (>=0.9999), monotonic_violations=0, duplicates_delivered=0, invalid_ohlc_delivered=0, synthetic_candles_delivered=0. Decision: SELECTED, rule FLOOR_ADMITTED_ONE, selected candidate_b_validated_ohlcv_pipeline, 'correctness decided and latency did not vote'. Elapsed: minutes, not seven days. PERSISTED: `scripts/record_market_data_measurement.py --recorded-by ... --resolve-config-from-aws` resolved SUPABASE_URL, EXCHANGE_ID, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and REDIS_URL from the real account (ap-southeast-1) and wrote the row -- Supabase returned HTTP/2 201 Created -- printing 'Selected source: candidate_b_validated_ohlcv_pipeline. Paper sessions can now start.' Candidate A was correctly NOT recorded (its ElastiCache endpoint times out from outside the VPC, and the tool's own rule is that 'recording unmeasured teaches the store nothing'). VERIFIED THROUGH THE PRODUCTION DECISION PATH, not by trusting the tool's exit: read back via `latest_measurements()` -> `select_market_data_source`, the exact code a session start calls, against production. Returns outcome=SELECTED, rule=FLOOR_ADMITTED_ONE, selected=candidate_b_validated_ohlcv_pipeline, blocked=False -- where `blocked` was True on every start before. Stored row: expected_bars=10,000, completeness=1.0, and zeros across monotonic/duplicates/invalid_ohlc/synthetic. PROVENANCE RECORDED ON THE ROW, deliberately: the measurement was taken from a development host, so its CORRECTNESS half is portable (those are properties of the venue's data and of the validator's code, not of the host) while its LATENCY half describes that host. It does not decide anything today -- with one admitted candidate latency did not vote -- but `recorded_by` says so rather than leaving a figure to be mistaken for production's. Regression: 219 passed across tests/test_rt04_measurement_store_round_trips.py, test_paper_market_feed_selection.py, test_market_data_source_decision.py and test_task_28_1_session_routes.py; the 7 perf-harness tests still skip behind their experiment_only guard and the module imports clean. ||| OPEN ON PR #85, NOT MERGED, AND NOT CLAIMED AS PASSING CI. The 'Unit & Integration Tests' job fails on that branch with exactly one failure, tests/property/test_protected_logic_containment.py::test_trace_and_export_surfaces_contain_no_protected_logic, while the same job SUCCEEDS on main (run 39987240090, commit ac11d030) -- so it is this branch, not flake: reproduced on a re-run of the identical commit. Everything else on the PR is green except 'Provisioning, Privilege Hardening & Tenant Isolation', which fails identically on main and is pre-existing. WHAT IS KNOWN. The crash signature is a library bug class: the collection shrinker's `short_circuit` tries `[zero] * min_size` for a text draw whose alphabet does not contain the zero character. WHAT WAS RULED OUT. That is a hypothesis, NOT a measurement, and it is recorded as such. NEXT STEP, cheapest first: get the real assertion rather than the shrinker's crash -- either run that one test under Python 3.11 locally, or land a no-shrink profile that CI actually schedules, then read the falsifying example. Do not merge #85 until the underlying failure is identified; a protected-logic containment property (Requirements 1.19, 2.19) is not something to merge past on the assumption that it is noise.

findings.title: No venue reconciliation: fills, partial fills and ambiguous submissions are never resolved against the exchange
findings.evidence: W-1b (OrderWatchdog cannot obtain an executor in production) fixed: _get_executor_for_order now builds a REAL per-tenant executor by reusing order_control._executor_for (the same stored-key -> get_exchange_executor -> connect() path RT-21's manual cancel uses), via app_state.vault. Made async; all three call sites (_reconcile_open_orders, _adjudicate_ambiguous_execution, _refresh_order_status) now await it. tests/test_rt16_watchdog_executor_is_real.py (5 tests) + test_d5_watchdog_adjudication_repair.py (updated, 17 passing/1 skipped) + a ~1100-test targeted regression (order/watchdog/reconcil/execution_guard/master_executor) all green this session. ADDITIONALLY this session (commit a4758e4): OrderWatchdog._reconcile_open_orders now calls a new _record_reconciliation_mismatch on every proven divergence (_has_order_changed true), writing to ReconciliationMismatchRepository.record_mismatch at severity MEDIUM, never CRITICAL -- closing the 'ReconciliationScheduler polls a table nothing writes' gap. tests/test_rt16_reconciliation_mismatches_are_recorded.py (4 tests, SQLite-backed): a real divergence writes exactly one MEDIUM row readable from a second session; an unchanged order writes nothing; the diverging field is named correctly; a write failure is logged and never breaks reconciliation. Regression: test_d5_watchdog_adjudication_repair.py + test_rt16_watchdog_executor_is_real.py + test_rt16_reconciliation_mismatches_are_recorded.py + test_rt04_measurement_store_round_trips.py + test_rt21_close_position_flattens_exposure.py (45 passed/1 skipped); full tests/test_validation_sweep.py + test_schema_table_reference_drift.py + test_task_28_1_session_routes.py (584 passed, 2 failed -- confirmed pre-existing on clean tree, unrelated billing-route findings, not caused by this change). FURTHER this session (commit 3c333e0): fixed ConsistencyChecker's three compounding problems that made it unsafe to ever enable, not one. _get_exchange_positions() now builds a real per-tenant executor via the same vault-based path (order_control._executor_for) RT-21/RT-16 already use, and reads get_balance() (the correct spot call) instead of the credential-less get_or_create_exchange() + fetch_positions() (a derivatives/margin call with nothing to read on this spot-only platform). _run_consistency_checks now checks result.error_message first, so a failed CHECK (exchange timeout, no credentials) is never treated as a confirmed mismatch and escalated. _handle_mismatch no longer calls GlobalKillSwitch.activate() (a true platform-wide halt) at all -- it now writes to the SAME ReconciliationMismatchRepository RT-16 gave OrderWatchdog a real caller for, at severity MEDIUM, never CRITICAL, so ReconciliationScheduler's own, already-correct severity gate decides whether anything escalates. tests/test_rt16_consistency_checker_is_safely_gated.py (8 tests, fakes: no real exchange, no network): real-executor+get_balance wiring; no-vault raises rather than a silent empty result; a failed check never reaches _handle_mismatch; a real mismatch is recorded at MEDIUM; the kill switch is never imported or called from this module at all. connection_engine.py's get_or_create_exchange docstring updated (no longer names this file as a credential-less caller). Full regression: targeted RT-16 suite (67 passed/12 skipped) + full validation_sweep/schema_drift (480 passed, 2 failed -- same pre-existing, unrelated billing findings). *** FILL EVIDENCE NOW REQUIRED FOR COMPLETED (this session). *** The remaining_action above named it: 'execution_records are still marked COMPLETED on venue accept rather than on a confirmed fill'. That is now fixed, and it was three defects compounding, not one. (1) STATUS. `execute_with_idempotency` wrote ExecutionStatus.COMPLETED whenever `_execute_trade_internal` reported success, and success at a venue means ACCEPTED, not FILLED -- a resting limit order and a genuine fill took the same branch. COMPLETED is operationally terminal: `OrderWatchdog._find_open_orders`, `_find_stale_orders` and `ExchangeReconciliation._get_active_orders` all select only PENDING/EXECUTING, so the row left every reconciliation population at the exact moment it most needed watching. (2) QUANTITY, and this is the one the finding's own description understated. `execution_engine.py` built the result with `float(result.filled_size or size)`. `0` is falsy in Python, so whenever the venue reported `filled=0` this substituted THE FULL REQUESTED SIZE as filled -- and `master_executor.settle_exposure` reads exactly that field to credit `recovered_exposure_coins`, the bot's only record of what it holds, while the fee row is computed from the same number. One falsy zero turned an unfilled order into phantom exposure AND a phantom fee. `float(result.avg_price or price)` had the identical bug, reporting the price we ASKED for as a price we GOT. (3) THE ROW WAS NOT WATCHABLE ANYWAY, so fixing the status alone would have been inert -- it would have swapped 'marked complete and never checked' for 'marked executing and never checked', which is worse. Every venue call in OrderWatchdog passed `order.order_id` and both population queries required `order_id IS NOT NULL`, but TRADE-12 deliberately moved the venue's identifier to `venue_order_id` (because `order_id` carries FOREIGN KEY -> orders(id)) and the engine leaves `order_id` NULL. So EVERY row the live engine created was invisible to the watchdog on both counts. Worse, `EventRouter._find_execution_by_order_id` matched the venue id taken from the exchange's own WebSocket event against `order_id` -- the platform column that never holds one -- so the fastest and most authoritative fill-confirmation path in the system resolved to None every time and the event was dropped as an unknown order. THE FIX. `classify_venue_fill` (core/models/execution_record.py) reads the venue's own status word and its own filled quantity and returns filled / partially_filled / accepted, resolving every ambiguous case to `accepted` -- under-reporting is self-correcting because the row stays EXECUTING and therefore stays in the watchdog's population, while over-reporting is not. `None` (the venue did not say) and `0` (the venue said none) are now distinguished, which is the whole defect. Only a confirmed full fill persists COMPLETED; `update_status` gained optional filled_size / avg_price / remaining_size / filled_at / exchange_status so the fill columns are actually written (they never were, so a COMPLETED row carried filled_size IS NULL and the watchdog's `fill_delta = new_filled - Decimal(order.filled_size or "0")` re-credited the entire quantity on the next poll). The engine returns 'accepted'/'partially_filled' instead of 'completed', so settle_exposure credits nothing for an unfilled order and the fee is 0. `settle_exposure` learned `partially_filled` (a real part fill is real exposure). master_executor's signal-trail write stopped being binary FILLED/FAILED, which would have recorded a LIVE resting order as FAILED. OrderWatchdog and EventRouter now resolve the venue id from `venue_order_id`, falling back to `order_id` for older recovery rows. NO NEW ExecutionStatus MEMBER, deliberately: `executionstatus` is a PostgreSQL enum (alembic d97ffff9c3bb) so SUBMITTED would need an ALTER TYPE, and EXECUTING already carries exactly this meaning everywhere else -- `_update_order_from_status` maps a venue partial fill onto it and `resolve_stale_execution` defaults its CAS to from_status=EXECUTING. ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN WORK, recorded because the test caught it and not me: I first made `settle_exposure` REFUSE to credit a `completed` result that carried no quantity, which broke tests/test_rt06_exposure_follows_completed_fills_only.py::test_completed_without_a_reported_size_uses_the_requested_quantity. The test is right and I was wrong. `previous_exposure` gates position limits, so OVER-stating it makes the bot trade less than it could, while UNDER-stating it makes the bot believe it has room it does not have and buy again -- refusing to credit a confirmed fill is the DANGEROUS direction. The phantom exposure came from the STATUS, not that fallback; with the status corrected an accepted order never reaches the crediting branch at all. Reverted, and the reasoning is now recorded at the fallback so it is not 'fixed' again. VERIFICATION. tests/test_rt16_completed_requires_a_confirmed_fill.py -- 29 tests, real engine, real repository, real in-memory SQLite execution_records, recording double for the venue. Includes a POSITIVE CONTROL (a confirmed fill still reaches COMPLETED, so the 'not completed' assertions cannot be passing because the harness cannot complete anything) and two NEGATIVE CONTROLS that assert the PRE-FIX watchdog filter and pre-fix EventRouter lookup find nothing, so those tests fail if the engine ever starts writing order_id and silently stops proving anything. Regression: 205 passed / 1 skipped across the RT-16/RT-06/RT-17/DUP-02/D5-watchdog/baseline/deploy01 suites; 3002 passed on the full execution+order+watchdog+signal selection. The 4 remaining failures in that selection were confirmed PRE-EXISTING by stashing the change and re-running on a clean tree, where they fail identically (test_db01_provisioning_order.py::test_024_comes_after_the_file_that_declares_referral_commissions and 3 in test_rt08_deployment_state_is_durable.py). tests/regression/baseline/live_order_path.json re-recorded under the harness's own authorisation mechanism with `_baseline_note_fill_evidence_required_rt16`; the diff is 12 insertions and 0 deletions, and the 4 pre-existing provenance notes (DUP-02, TRADE-01, RT-17, TRADE-12) were carried forward explicitly -- a plain re-record would have silently deleted them, since write_baseline overwrites the file with a freshly captured payload.

findings.title: Manual paper orders fill at hardcoded reference prices or at a price the client supplies for a market order
findings.evidence: Containment (earlier): hardcoded reference prices and client price for market orders removed; market orders refused (409 PAPER_MARKET_DATA_UNAVAILABLE) without a measured quote; tests/test_paper02_market_orders_need_measured_price.py (5). THIS SESSION (commit 0e754cc): get_fresh_market_price now reads a real last-price cache instead of unconditionally returning None. mds/main.py::broadcast_ohlcv -- the same loop that republishes every real CCXT candle for every Paper_Session's validated feed, on both its websocket and REST-fallback paths -- now additionally writes a durable, 150s-TTL'd mds:last_price:{exchange}:{symbol} cache entry alongside each existing publish (no second market-data path, no new exchange connection, no credentials). get_fresh_market_price reads that cache for a fixed default exchange ("binance", matching mds/main.py's own existing fallback default) and returns None -- never a fabricated or stale price -- for every case but a real, unexpired cached value. The key format is spelled as a literal in both files (the same convention this codebase already uses for TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET/TRANSPORT_REST, since mds/main.py is a standalone microservice process), held equal by a test. tests/test_paper02_fresh_market_price.py (9 tests, fakes: no network, no real exchange, no real Redis): key-format agreement; broadcast_ohlcv writes the cache on a real websocket tick and a real REST-fallback tick, with the TTL; a cached price round-trips as an exact Decimal; no cached entry, a cache read failure, an unreadable payload, and a non-numeric cached price are all read as None, never an exception; the pre-existing no-mocking pin still holds. Regression: 401 tests across the targeted paper-trading suite + full validation_sweep/schema_drift/import-resolution (482 passed, 2 failed -- same pre-existing, unrelated billing findings) both clean; a broader "-k paper or market_data or mds" sweep is flaky independent of this change (reproduced identically against a clean stash of the same commit). ||| CLOSED (Kiro), AND THE PREVIOUS FIX WAS INERT -- MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. This entry recorded 'a manual market order now succeeds ONLY for a symbol some active Paper_Session ... is already streaming'. The first half was FALSE: it succeeded for no symbol at all. `place_order` normalises with `_clean_symbol` (upper().replace('/', '-') -> 'BTC-USDT') and looked the cache up under THAT form, while mds/main.py keys the cache on the symbol the subscribe command named -- for a Paper_Session the ccxt market symbol 'BTC/USDT'. Verified directly before changing anything, by running both key builders on what place_order actually passes: writer 'mds:last_price:binance:BTC/USDT' vs reader 'mds:last_price:binance:BTC-USDT'. The keys could never match, so EVERY manual market order refused with NO_FRESH_PRICE regardless of what was streaming. WHY THE TESTS PASSED THROUGHOUT: they call `get_fresh_market_price('BTC/USDT')` directly with an already-slashed symbol, bypassing `_clean_symbol` -- so they exercised the key FORMAT, which was always consistent between writer and reader (and which test_the_key_format_agrees_between_writer_and_reader pins), and never the symbol FORM that reaches it from a real order. SECOND DEFECT, same area: the reader hardcoded 'binance' while a Paper_Session runs on DEFAULT_EXCHANGE, so any deployment on another venue wrote keys this reader never looked at. `_paper_price_exchange()` now reads DEFAULT_EXCHANGE, keeping 'binance' only as the fallback -- which is not invented: it is the same fallback mds/main.py::handle_commands itself uses for a subscribe naming no exchange. THE RECORDED BLOCKER WAS THE WRONG QUESTION. It was: watch_ohlcv on a 1m timeframe 'can legitimately take up to a minute to yield its first candle', not a bound an inside-an-HTTP-request call can wait on, and this sandbox has 'no reachable exchange to measure that against'. Both halves are addressed rather than argued with. The venue IS reachable. And the premise is sidestepped: a candle stream withholds its first value until a bar CLOSES, whereas a ticker read returns the current last price immediately -- so the on-demand path asks for a PRICE, not a CANDLE, and the minute-long wait never arises. MEASURED against the live venue (ccxt binance fetch_ticker, 36 warm calls across BTC/ETH/DOGE, zero failures): median 201 ms, p95 ~516 ms, p99 516 ms; cold first call 6,105 ms. The bound is 3 s -- ~5.8x the warm p99, and deliberately BELOW the cold-start cost, so the first order in a fresh process refuses honestly rather than holding an HTTP worker for six seconds, leaving a warm pooled client behind. A refusal is always safe: it is the existing NO_FRESH_PRICE answer, and the point of PAPER-02 is that refusing beats inventing. So this is SUBSCRIBE-AND-DON'T-WAIT: the order is priced from REST, and a subscribe is published to mds:commands so the NEXT order for that symbol is served from the cache at no venue cost -- reusing paper_market_feed.mds_command rather than spelling the wire contract a third time. Not a second market-data path in the sense Requirement 14.2 forbids: it is the same REST read broadcast_ohlcv already falls back to, through the platform's single venue-client factory (connection_engine.get_or_create_exchange under the public credential-less pool identity routers/market.py already uses). No new credentials, no new connection management, no socket. The mock refusal is not optional here -- _apply_mock_interface.fetch_ticker returns a HARDCODED price, so filling from it would reinstate this finding's original defect by a new route; a mock-served connection returns None, the same check open_feed makes for Requirement 14.8. COMPATIBILITY: `get_fresh_market_price` keeps its name, signature and cache-only semantics, and `resolve_market_price` calls it through the module global -- so conftest's `fresh_paper_quote` fixture still short-circuits the venue path unchanged for the ~13 suites that depend on it. A new autouse conftest guard neutralises `fetch_venue_quote` suite-wide, because conftest sets DEFAULT_EXCHANGE=binance globally and without it every market-order test would reach the live venue; production behaviour is therefore opt-IN for a test, the same shape fresh_paper_quote already has for the cache half. One existing assertion updated rather than bent: a source-inspection test asserted place_order mentions `get_fresh_market_price`; it now names `resolve_market_price`, the seam the order path calls, and additionally asserts the client's price cannot reach the market branch. A test was added pinning that resolve_market_price consults the cache BEFORE the venue, since that ordering is what keeps the venue read rare. Regression: 24 new tests (tests/test_paper02_on_demand_quote.py) -- 23 offline plus one live-venue test, skipped unless PAPER02_LIVE_VENUE=1, RUN HERE AND PASSING: a real BTC/USDT quote resolved within the bound and range-checked. 2236 passed / 164 skipped across the whole paper/risk/tenant-isolation/notification/live-execution/baseline selection. No order is placed at a venue by any of this: paper trading reaches a venue only to read a price. ||| OPEN ON PR #85, NOT MERGED, AND NOT CLAIMED AS PASSING CI. The 'Unit & Integration Tests' job fails on that branch with exactly one failure, tests/property/test_protected_logic_containment.py::test_trace_and_export_surfaces_contain_no_protected_logic, while the same job SUCCEEDS on main (run 39987240090, commit ac11d030) -- so it is this branch, not flake: reproduced on a re-run of the identical commit. Everything else on the PR is green except 'Provisioning, Privilege Hardening & Tenant Isolation', which fails identically on main and is pre-existing. WHAT IS KNOWN. The reported error is NOT an assertion from the test: it is `ValueError: 48 is not in list` raised inside Hypothesis itself, at `internal/intervalsets.py:107` via `index_from_char_in_shrink_order` (48 is ord('0')), reached from `engine.shrink_interesting_test_cases` -> `greedy_shrink` -> `minimize_individual_choices`. Two consequences: (1) Hypothesis DID find a failing example -- shrinking only runs on an interesting case -- and (2) the shrinker's own crash MASKS whatever that example asserted, so the actual defect is still unseen. The crash signature is a library bug class: the collection shrinker's `short_circuit` tries `[zero] * min_size` for a text draw whose alphabet does not contain the zero character. WHAT WAS RULED OUT. Not reproducible locally: 5 consecutive whole-file runs, 3 explicit --hypothesis-seed values, then a 24-seed sweep with the shrink phase disabled -- all passed. Local Python is 3.12.10; CI is 3.11.17, with hypothesis pinned to the SAME 6.165.10 in both, so a version skew is excluded and the difference is the interpreter or the environment. A first hypothesis -- that the new autouse `_no_on_demand_venue_quotes` guard in tests/conftest.py was function-scoped and therefore wrapped every Hypothesis `@given` test -- was WRONG: it was changed to session scope (commit 49f29660, which is better engineering regardless: one substitution instead of fifteen thousand) and CI failed again identically. A temporary no-shrink profile was pushed to make CI print the real assertion; GitHub Actions never scheduled a run for that commit, so it yielded nothing and was reverted rather than left in. WHY A CAUSAL LINK TO THIS SESSION'S CHANGES IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The failing test exercises `strategy_operations.preview_node` and `compare_versions` for a NON-OWNER, NON-ENTITLED caller, whose authorisation refusal is reached before any market-data work; `_preview_data_quality` is called at strategy_operations.py:5030, downstream of that refusal. Neither the outlier policy nor the paper price path is reachable there. The likelier mechanism is indirect: two new test modules change collection, which changes Hypothesis's example stream, which surfaces a LATENT counterexample main's stream happened to miss. That is a hypothesis, NOT a measurement, and it is recorded as such. NEXT STEP, cheapest first: get the real assertion rather than the shrinker's crash -- either run that one test under Python 3.11 locally, or land a no-shrink profile that CI actually schedules, then read the falsifying example. Do not merge #85 until the underlying failure is identified; a protected-logic containment property (Requirements 1.19, 2.19) is not something to merge past on the assumption that it is noise.

findings.evidence: MarketplaceExpiryWorker added to local.worker_definitions in terraform/ecs.tf (task definition + ECS service via for_each); tests/test_worker_deployment_coverage.py ledger updated ADDITIONALLY this session (commit 6aa0ac9): investigated this entry's own remaining_action ('image pinning (workers use vyomquant-api:latest)') in more depth and found it understates the real gap, with a direct interaction with this session's own earlier CI-02 fix. terraform/ecs.tf's worker task definitions ALL reference vyomquant-api:latest ('Workers use the backend image', per that file's own comment), and grepped scripts/ecs_deploy_and_diagnose.py (the actual CI/CD deploy engine 03-deploy.yml runs) end to end: it only ever targets ECS_SERVICE, hardcoded to the API service -- nothing anywhere updates a WORKER service's task definition. CI-02's own fix (commit 2d1502b) correctly stopped 02-build.yml from pushing that mutable tag at all, since nothing was SUPPOSED to depend on it -- which silently removed the only mechanism that ever updated a worker's code, a regression closed here by giving workers an explicit, correct update path instead of relying on a tag that should not have existed as a dependency in the first place. Added get_service_task_definition_arn/list_worker_services (discovers worker services by the 'vyomquant-worker-' prefix via `aws ecs list-services`, not hardcoded keys, so OPS-TRAIN-01's `training` entry and any future worker need no second place updated)/register_worker_task_definition (same 'change only the image' shape as the existing API-specific register_task_definition, but sets it on every container and deliberately skips validate_critical_config, which asserts API-shaped config -- port 8000/cpu 1024/mem 2048/the full API secret set -- none of which describes a worker)/redeploy_workers (loops over every discovered worker, best-effort and isolated per worker). New TestWorkerRedeployment class (8 tests) + a fix to the existing test_execute_deployment_success_flow, which would otherwise have made a real, unmocked `aws ecs list-services` subprocess call from inside a unit test (caught by it actually running and failing fast on missing credentials, not by a clean assertion). Full regression: tests/test_ecs_deploy_rollback.py (25 passed, up from 18) + tests/test_validation_sweep.py + tests/test_worker_deployment_coverage.py (408 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed). ||| CORRECTION (Kiro, forced by the RECON-01 investigation). This entry records the terraform-state blocker as 'deliberately not done without asking first -- new shared infra', which frames it as MY CAUTION and implies owner approval would unblock it. That is wrong, and it matters because it sends the owner to the wrong remedy. MEASURED directly against the real account just now: identity is arn:aws:iam::273709947018:user/github-actions; `s3api head-bucket --bucket vyomquant-terraform-state` returns 404 Not Found (the bucket genuinely does not exist, consistent with what was recorded); and `s3api create-bucket` returns AccessDenied -- verbatim: 'User: arn:aws:iam::273709947018:user/github-actions is not authorized to perform: s3:CreateBucket on resource ... because no identity-based policy allows the s3:CreateBucket action'. The probe bucket was consequently NOT created, so no stray infrastructure was left behind. Also denied for this identity, tested the same way: s3:ListAllMyBuckets, events:ListRules (so an EventBridge scheduled task is not an available workaround either), and iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy (so the envelope cannot be enumerated statically and has to be probed call by call). SO THE REMEDY IS NOT 'ASK THE OWNER FOR PERMISSION TO PROCEED'. It is: either attach s3:CreateBucket (plus DynamoDB table creation for the lock table) to the deploy identity, or have the owner bootstrap the state bucket + lock table once with a stronger identity, or run terraform with local state. Until one of those happens, no agent or CI job using user/github-actions can create the worker services this entry is about, with or without approval.

The `token` parameter was accepted but never read. Fixed: client.auth.admin.sign_out(jwt=current_user['access_token'], scope='global') against a service-role client (get_service_supabase), which makes a real server-to-server revocation naming WHOSE session to end. tests/test_auth01_signout_revokes_the_real_session.py (4 tests): admin sign-out called with the caller's own token and scope='global'; no service-role client is a clean 503 not a fake success; an admin API failure is a 400; auth is still required. Regression: targeted suite + full validation_sweep/schema_drift (484 passed, 2 failed -- same pre-existing, unrelated billing findings) + an 80-test auth/websocket sweep all clean. Commit b3701ba.
