findings.title: Any access_token in the URL hash becomes the session (login CSRF)
findings.evidence:
Switched the Supabase client to PKCE: src/supabase.js now passes flowType: 'pkce' to createClient (alongside the pre-existing persistSession/autoRefreshToken/detectSessionInUrl: true). This is the actual fix the prior FE-01 pass (commit 83c8a8c) identified but did not attempt. A legitimate OAuth (signInWithOAuth) / magic-link (signInWithOtp) / sign-up-confirmation (signUp) redirect now lands as '?code=...' instead of '#access_token=...', and @supabase/auth-js only exchanges that code for a session if THIS browser also holds the matching code_verifier it generated locally when the flow started -- confirmed by reading node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js: _isPKCECallback requires both params.code AND a stored '<storageKey>-code-verifier'; an attacker's own valid code has no verifier in the victim's browser, so exchangeCodeForSession fails and no session is adopted. Also confirmed, in that same source, a second-order effect: with flowType:'pkce' configured, _getSessionFromURL now actively throws AuthPKCEGrantCodeExchangeError('Not a valid PKCE flow url.') on a stray '#access_token=' hash (a flow-type mismatch) instead of silently adopting it. This matters because the prior FE-01 pass's path-allowlist narrowing of this app's OWN hand-rolled hash parsing (getEffectiveToken/PasswordRecoveryHandler) never touched the BIGGER hole: supabase-js's own detectSessionInUrl independently adopts an implicit hash on ANY route the instant the page loads, before any app/router code runs, and bridges the resulting SIGNED_IN event into this app's sessionStorage via the onAuthStateChange listener already present in PasswordRecoveryHandler -- regardless of the app-level path allowlist. PKCE closes that SDK-level path too, not just this app's own duplicate of it; this escalates the original finding's severity assessment of how exploitable the pre-PKCE implicit flow actually was.

Updated every dependent path in src/App.jsx: (1) renamed _isLegitimateAuthHashLandingPath -> _isLegitimateAuthRedirectLandingPath (same 4-path allowlist: AUTH_REDIRECT_PATH/signin/signup/root), since it now gates a '?code=' query param, not a hash; (2) getEffectiveToken() no longer reads window.location.hash at all -- the manual access_token-adoption branch (both the original unconditional version and the first FE-01 pass's path-allowlisted version) is deleted outright, not re-narrowed, since a legitimate redirect never produces that shape under PKCE and the SDK itself now refuses it; (3) added hasPendingAuthCodeExchange() and a new useGuardedAuthToken() hook so AuthGuard/GuestGuard correctly handle that a PKCE exchange is an async network round-trip (exchangeCodeForSession), unlike the old synchronous hash read: on first render of an allowlisted path carrying '?code=', the guards now show a brief 'Completing sign-in...' state and await supabase.auth.getSession() (which awaits the SDK's own initializePromise -- confirmed in GoTrueClient.js) rather than bouncing an arriving user to /signin before the exchange has resolved -- a behaviour change the task's own brief anticipated ('the client library handles the exchange differently'). (4) PasswordRecoveryHandler's own non-recovery access_token-from-hash branch is deleted (dead code under PKCE), replaced by a branch that forwards a resolving '?code=' landing on '/', '/signin' or '/signup' to AUTH_REDIRECT_PATH once supabase.auth.getSession() confirms a session -- mirroring what the deleted hash branch used to do for those same three paths. Its type=recovery branch is UNCHANGED (still hash-based, still outside this app's control): re-confirmed this session that src/ has no resetPasswordForEmail call site anywhere, and found no 'forgot password' UI entry point either, so this frontend still neither generates nor can safely allowlist that email's redirect.

NEW RISK IDENTIFIED AND DOCUMENTED IN CODE (src/supabase.js, PasswordRecoveryHandler): switching this client's flowType to 'pkce' means supabase-js's OWN internal session detection will now REJECT an implicit-shaped '#access_token=...&type=recovery' hash as a flow-type mismatch rather than silently adopting it into its real internal session -- and supabase.auth.updateUser() on /reset-password needs THAT internal session (confirmed in GoTrueClient.js: _updateUser throws AuthSessionMissingError without one), not just this app's own hand-rolled sessionStorage bookkeeping. findings.title: The web app is served without a Content-Security-Policy
findings.evidence: Confirmed by reading algo22-terminal/index.html and .github/workflows/06-frontend-deploy.yml: this SPA is built by Vite and synced straight to an S3 bucket behind CloudFront (no origin server at request time, unlike the API's own SecurityHeadersMiddleware in backend_app/main.py, which already sends a tightened nonce+hash CSP but only on backend-served responses) -- index.html carried no CSP at all, meta or header, and could not easily be given one without weakening it: three inline <script> blocks (local-dev detection, a Sentry loader, a GA/Clarity loader) would have forced 'unsafe-inline' into script-src the moment a CSP was added, which defeats most of what a CSP is for. Fixed both problems together. (1) The three inline scripts moved verbatim (same isDummy/local-detection/loader logic, now reading import.meta.env.VITE_* instead of index.html's %VITE_X% token substitution -- equivalent at build time, Vite's native mechanism either way) into algo22-terminal/src/bootstrap.js, a same-origin ES module loaded via <script type="module" src="/src/bootstrap.js"> ahead of main.jsx -- already covered by script-src 'self' with no extra grant needed. (2) index.html now carries <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> with script-src 'self' plus only the origins this build actually loads scripts from (confirmed by grep of src/: js.sentry-cdn.com, www.googletagmanager.com, www.clarity.ms, checkout.razorpay.com for the one real payment path this platform has -- Stripe origins deliberately excluded, since src/pages/Billing.jsx documents this deployment has no live Stripe secret and every Stripe-only endpoint 500s by design) -- no unsafe-inline, no unsafe-eval anywhere in the policy. connect-src covers every API-hostname topology the deploy workflow's own allow-list names (same-origin CloudFront proxy, api.vyomquant.in, or the raw CloudFront domain) plus the wildcarded Supabase, Sentry, Clarity and GA hosts the app actually calls. A meta-tag CSP cannot carry frame-ancestors/sandbox/report-uri (browsers ignore those three outside an HTTP header per the HTML spec) -- documented in index.html's own comment and left to INF-02 (terraform does not describe the production deployment; a CloudFront response-headers policy is the real fix for that gap, and this session has no AWS credentials to apply one even if terraform described the live distribution). New tests/unit/csp_fe02.test.js (11 tests): the CSP meta tag exists; script-src is 'self' plus https-only named origins with no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and no directive left empty; every remaining <script> tag in index.html either names a same-origin src or is the non-executable application/ld+json block (browsers do not run it as script and CSP's script-src does not gate it); bootstrap.js loads before main.jsx in document order; bootstrap.js's isDummyValue/detectLocal/runBootstrap reproduce the exact old inline-script behaviour (dummy/placeholder/test/unset id -> harmless local-only stub and no third-party script injected; a real-looking id -> the real Sentry/GA/Clarity loader script injected with that id). `npm run build` with the real Vite config still produces a working dist/index.html carrying the CSP meta tag and zero occurrences of VITE_SENTRY_DSN/VITE_GA_TRACKING_ID/VITE_CLARITY_PROJECT_ID (confirming the token substitution moved to bootstrap.js's bundled output correctly, verified by grepping the emitted entry chunk for __VQ_LOCAL__/clarity.ms/sentry-cdn, all present).
findings.remaining_action: This closes the "served without a CSP" gap in the one place this session can reach (the committed index.html). NOT done: a CloudFront response-headers policy or ALB header (the HTTP-header form of CSP, which alone can add frame-ancestors for real clickjacking protection and survives even if a future edit strips the meta tag) -- that is infrastructure this session has no AWS credentials to touch and that INF-02 already records as undescribed by the repo's own terraform. The remediation note's 'attach WAF, enable logging' half is unchanged for the same reason.

findings.evidence: LEDGER BOOKKEEPING FIX (no new code this pass): the fix_commit field was left as the literal placeholder string '(this commit)', never replaced with the real hash, and verification_level was left at 'code' even though real regression tests for this exact fix already exist and pass. PRODUCT DECISION this session: asked the product owner directly whether MFA enrollment is required/offered before a user's first payment today, since that determines whether gating billing/payment mutations behind AAL2 is a safe, narrow fix or would lock out every current paying user. Answer: 'for launch hold this feature' -- an explicit instruction to defer AAL2 gating on the billing routes (add_payment_method, delete_payment_method, create_checkout_session, verify_razorpay_payment, create_portal_session, cancel_subscription, resume_subscription), not to implement it this pass. RE-CONFIRMED this session: the user (acting as product owner) was asked to reconsider this hold given everything else completed this session, and explicitly reaffirmed it -- 'put it on hold for now, as a payment aggregator, Razorpay already has its own security checks.' No code changed as a result of this reconfirmation -- recording the decision and its actual scope accurately, not acting on it, per this entry's own standing instruction below.

findings.remaining_action: RESOLVED with real evidence this session, both halves of the question this entry's own evidence said terraform/ could not answer. (1) Is there a CDN in front of the ALB? CONFIRMED YES -- `cloudfront ListDistributions`/`GetDistribution` (live scoped CI credential) show a real distribution (id EEOXECPHQ8SR0, aliases www.vyomquant.in/app.vyomquant.in/vyomquant.in) with an ALB origin (`vyomquant-alb-...elb.amazonaws.com`, http-only) and 5 cache behaviors forwarding `/ws/*`, `/api/*`, `/health*`, `/metrics*` and `/openapi.json` to that ALB origin. Confirmed `/api/billing/webhook/stripe` and `/api/billing/webhook/razorpay` (grepped billing.py's own route decorators) both fall under the `/api/*` behavior, so genuine provider webhooks really do transit CloudFront -- public DNS resolution of app.vyomquant.in/www.vyomquant.in lands in AWS's published CloudFront edge IP range, independently corroborating this from outside AWS's own API. terraform/cloudfront.tf's source (one distribution, S3-only, no ALB behavior) does NOT match this -- the same class of INF-02 drift, now confirmed for a second resource type. (2) Is the real running TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS set correctly for that topology (2: CloudFront + ALB, per this function's own code comment)? CHECKED DIRECTLY against the real task definition the API service is running (`ecs DescribeServices` -> `vyomquant-api:214` -> `ecs DescribeTaskDefinition`): TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=2 is already set in the container's environment -- correct for the real topology just confirmed, not the code's own fail-safe default of 1. So genuine Stripe/Razorpay webhooks are NOT being misattributed/rejected in production today on hop-count grounds; whoever provisioned this task definition already got this right, even though no source in this repository (terraform or otherwise) documents why 2 is the correct value or where CloudFront's ALB behavior comes from. findings.title: Hardcoded static HMAC secret in the live-order authorization gate
findings.evidence: Both core/live_execution_gate._GATE_SECRET and core/global_safety._VALIDATION_SECRET (an identical, previously-undocumented sibling bug the audit's remaining_action did not separately name) were hardcoded bytes literals in source. Both now os.urandom(32), generated fresh at module import -- safe because mint and verify for each are always called from the same synchronous order-placement call stack in the same process (traced: execution_engine.py -> exchange_executor.py/transactional_execution_manager.py for both), never persisted or read back across a restart or by a different process, so a per-process random key loses nothing a fixed one provided while closing the actual gap (unreadable from source, rotates automatically with no operator/deployment action needed -- stronger than the suggested env-var approach, which would need ops to configure and rotate it). tests/test_sec13_gate_secrets_are_not_hardcoded.py (5 tests): neither secret is the old literal; each is 32 random bytes; three real subprocesses get three different secrets; mint-then-verify still agrees within one process (the control this must not break); the two secrets stay independent. Regression: test_trade04 suite (62 tests) + a 274-test safety/execution-engine/kill-switch sweep + full validation_sweep/schema_drift (480 passed, 2 failed -- same pre-existing, unrelated billing findings) all clean. Commit ca63faf.
findings.remaining_action: Closed as designed: a per-process-random secret is the correct fix here specifically because neither artefact is ever persisted or verified across a restart/process boundary (confirmed by tracing every call site) -- NOT because an env-var-sourced, cross-process rotatable secret (as originally suggested) was attempted and found wanting. If a future change ever persists a LiveOrderAuthorization or a validation token across a restart (e.g. to support resuming an in-flight order after a crash), this reasoning would need revisiting before that change ships, since a restart would then invalidate an authorization minted just before it.

findings.title: In-app legal documents are stub text that contradicts the product's actual behavior
findings.evidence: INVESTIGATED THIS SESSION, deliberately NOT fixed. Confirmed the exact contradiction the title names: algo22-terminal/src/pages/LegalPage.jsx's Terms of Service section 1 states unconditionally, as static authored copy with no data binding of any kind (confirmed by that file's own module docstring: 'there is no READ on this page... no api.* call, no supabase call, not even a mutation'), that 'the Beta Service uses simulated balances and does not perform live trades on real exchange accounts' and 'NO REAL MONETARY TRANSACTIONS OR DEPLOYMENTS'. This is flatly false once live trading is enabled: RT-15 (this ledger's own earlier finding, VERIFIED_FIXED) hard-gates REAL live order execution at backend_app/core/live_execution_gate.py's assert_platform_live_trading_enabled, and backend_app/main.py's own /api/system/trading-capabilities endpoint exists specifically to tell the frontend 'whether LIVE execution is available on this platform' -- i.e. live trading is a real, built, gated, sometimes-on feature, not a hypothetical. Grepped LegalPage.jsx and App.jsx for any reference to live_trading_available/trading-capabilities: none. The legal document a user agrees to makes an absolute, static claim about trading mode that the system itself knows, via an endpoint it already exposes, can be false. The contradiction is real and is exactly as the title states. ESCALATION this session: asked the product owner directly whether live (real-money) trading is currently offered to real users today, specifically to resolve this entry's own named open question ('a decision on whether the product even offers live trading publicly yet'). Answer received: YES, live trading is offered to real users today. This changes this finding's own urgency assessment materially: the in-app legal documents' contradiction with actual product behaviour is not a pre-launch defect to clear before going live -- it is a PRESENT-TENSE gap while real users' real money is already at risk under documents that do not accurately disclose that risk. Escalating priority/severity accordingly. This does not change what this session is authorised to do about it: editing live legal-document text or risk-disclosure claims unilaterally remains out of scope for the same reason stated below (no legal authority, no counsel engaged) -- if anything, the stakes being confirmed real make an ad hoc, unreviewed edit MORE dangerous, not less, since a wrong or incomplete disclosure fix could create a new, worse liability than the stale text it replaced. Recorded here so this is not silently downgraded by its own pre-existing P2/Medium rating, and surfaced directly to the user in this session's own response rather than left for a reader of this ledger alone to notice. INTERIM STOPGAP applied this session (commit 635d32a), explicitly requested and approved by the product owner after being shown the exact diff and the limitation it carries, pending real counsel: removed the ToS's specific false claims (the '& Paper Trading Only' heading qualifier, 'solely... paper trading' from the opening sentence, and the 'NO REAL MONETARY TRANSACTIONS OR DEPLOYMENTS' bullet entirely). Deliberately added NO new disclosure language in their place, per the product owner's own explicit instruction and because drafting adequate live-trading risk disclosure is a legal-counsel decision this session has no standing to make unilaterally. The Risk Disclosure tab's 'Simulated / Paper Trading Limitations' section is unchanged -- it was already true and never claimed anything about live trading either way, so this stopgap did not touch it. ENGINEERING HALF COMPLETE, 2026-10-23, WITH PRODUCT-OWNER ANSWERS TO A 17-QUESTION INTAKE. The documents are now accurate, complete, single-sourced and version-tracked; what remains is counsel review and four placeholders only the owner can fill. DECISIONS TAKEN (owner's answers): Indian Private Limited company; governing law India with venue at Orai, Uttar Pradesh; registered address Mohammdabad, Orai, Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh; global signups; GDPR/UK-GDPR language included; 18+; live trading WILL launch; Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity retained; API-key statement corrected to the truth; no refunds except where law requires; Razorpay purchases are fixed-term and non-renewing; creators responsible for their own taxes; GST INCLUSIVE; cross-border transfer to Singapore disclosed rather than migrated; 30-day deletion; acceptance tracking built in full; duplicate legal page deleted. ONE ANSWER WAS CORRECTED WITH EVIDENCE RATHER THAN IMPLEMENTED AS GIVEN. The owner initially answered GST-EXCLUSIVE (13=B) and stated twice that 'Razorpay will calculate GST on billing'. That is false for this integration and would have broken checkout: razorpayCheckout.js uses STANDARD CHECKOUT, which charges the exact server-created order amount ('Razorpay takes the authoritative amount from the order'), and billing.py's SEC-02 guard `_reconcile_razorpay_payment_with_order` RAISES RazorpayOrderMismatch when `order.amount != payment.amount`. So a gateway-added 18% would have produced a 58,882-paise payment against a 49,900-paise order, the webhook would have refused to grant the plan, and the customer would have been charged for nothing. What Razorpay does automatically is charge GST on ITS OWN FEE to the merchant, which is not GST collected from the end customer. Presented both options with costs; owner moved to INCLUSIVE, which is true today and needs no code change. GST-exclusive would require GST computation in subscription_engine.py, changed order amounts, an updated mismatch guard and HSN/SAC tax invoices -- recorded as a separate piece of work, not done. A FOURTH FALSE STATEMENT WAS FOUND, by a test rather than by reading. The finding named three; `test_no_component_declares_its_own_legal_prose` surfaced a fourth copy of legally-operative text in components/landing/Footer.jsx, which said 'Paper trading mode is enabled by default' (implying live trading is a switch the reader can flip, when it is operator-granted per account -- the SAME false implication the ToS carried, in a second place, which is how the first survived) and 'all execution decisions are made by the user', which is the opposite of the central risk on an automated platform: the user chooses the strategy, and the strategy then places orders unprompted. Both corrected and single-sourced as SUMMARY_DISCLAIMER. THE TWO DIVERGENT DOCUMENT SETS ARE NOW ONE. components/legal/LegalPage.jsx held the prose inline AND src/pages/LegalPage.jsx held a second, different set; both were routed and served, and they CONTRADICTED each other on a material commercial term -- components/legal promised 'pro-rated service credits', pages/LegalPage said 'All purchases are final and non-refundable' (its line 312). Which page a customer happened to open decided whether they were owed money. pages/LegalPage.jsx is DELETED, /legal redirects to /legal/terms so existing links keep working, and everything renders from algo22-terminal/src/legal/documents.js. ACCEPTANCE TRACKING IS BUILT AND LIVE IN PRODUCTION. Migration 052_legal_acceptance.sql applied after a trial-then-rollback (browser write surface unchanged at 143 grants both times) and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: table present with all 8 columns, uq_legal_acceptances_user_version in place, RLS enabled, anon holds NO privilege at all, authenticated may SELECT only, and APPEND-ONLY IS PROVEN RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED -- both UPDATE and DELETE were attempted against a sentinel row and both were refused by trg_legal_acceptances_append_only. A repeat insert was confirmed idempotent. 182 existing profiles have no acceptance row, so all 182 will be prompted once, which is the correct answer for every account created before the mechanism existed. The server does NOT trust the client's version string: core/legal_documents.py holds its own LEGAL_VERSION, refuses an unpublished version with a 409 naming the current one, and refuses partial acceptance outright rather than storing it. tests/test_legal01_documents_and_acceptance.py asserts the frontend and backend version constants agree, so a one-sided bump cannot record agreement to text the other side never had. Signup now POSTs the acceptance after OTP verification -- the only point in that flow where a session exists, since the password step deliberately signs out. ANALYTICS NOW REQUIRE CONSENT. Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity previously loaded on first paint, before any interaction, while the Privacy Policy claimed 'We do not use third-party tracking or advertising cookies'. With global signups and GDPR language both in scope, disclosure alone is not consent. src/legal/consent.js defaults to DENIED (tests for an explicit grant rather than the absence of a refusal), bootstrap.js injects nothing until consent and installs inert stubs that DROP rather than queue events so a later grant cannot replay pre-consent behaviour, and CookieConsent.jsx gives Accept and Reject equal prominence with no pre-ticked box and no cookie wall. Sentry is deliberately NOT gated: it is error diagnostics under legitimate interest, declared as such, and gating crash reporting would lose the crashes of exactly the visitors who never answer a banner. Withdrawal is honest about its one limit -- it stops further sending but cannot unload an already-executed tag without a reload, which both the module and the Policy state. VERIFICATION: 356 tests pass (28 new LEGAL-01 tests plus test_no_secrets_in_bundle, test_sec06_no_hardcoded_supabase_jwt_in_scripts, test_schema_table_reference_drift, test_migration_tooling); `npx vite build` succeeds; eslint reports 0 errors on every touched file; the full FastAPI app imports with /api/legal/current, /api/legal/acceptance and /api/legal/accept mounted. ENTITY DETAILS SUPPLIED AND VALIDATED, AND THE TWO CONTROL GAPS CLOSED, 2026-10-23. ALL FOUR PLACEHOLDERS ARE GONE. The product owner supplied them and each was validated before publication, because a wrong statutory identifier in a Terms of Service is WORSE than a placeholder: a placeholder is visibly unfinished, a wrong number looks finished. legalName='Aerora Dynamics Private Limited' (corroborated independently -- src/utils/razorpayCheckout.js already defaults the checkout merchant name to 'Aerora Dynamics'); CIN='U26515UP2024PTC206131', parsed to U/26515/UP/2024/PTC/206131 with the state agreeing with the registered address and the ownership code PTC agreeing with the declared Private Limited form; GSTIN='09ABBCA0242R1ZI', whose CHECK DIGIT WAS COMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY VIA THE MOD-36 ALGORITHM AND AGREES ('I'), with state code 09 = Uttar Pradesh matching the address and the PAN's 4th character 'C' = Company matching a Pvt Ltd; PIN='285122', consistent with a Mohammdabad locality in Jalaun district (285001 is Orai town itself). The PIN is now embedded in ENTITY.address in Indian postal order rather than concatenated at three call sites, and the CIN and GSTIN -- previously DEFINED BUT NEVER RENDERED -- are now published in Terms section 1, which the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 expect of a GST-registered seller. ONE OBSERVATION RECORDED FOR COUNSEL RATHER THAN QUIETLY ACCEPTED: the CIN's industry code 26515 sits in the instruments and measuring-devices range, not software or financial services. That is a fact about the incorporation and not an error in these documents, but a reviewer will reasonably ask whether the registered object covers operating a trading platform. Added to REVIEW_NOTES. CONTROL GAP 1 CLOSED -- RESTRICTED JURISDICTIONS. Terms section 3 required the user not to be in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction, signups are global, and NOTHING IN CODE CHECKED IT: the clause was a sentence with no mechanism, which is the same defect class this whole finding is about. backend_app/core/restricted_jurisdictions.py now enforces it at signup (CU, IR, KP, SY -- the comprehensive programmes the clause's own wording describes) and the declaration is recorded on the acceptance row. IT IS DELIBERATELY DESCRIBED AS A DECLARED-COUNTRY GATE AND NOT AS SANCTIONS SCREENING, in the module docstring, the migration comment and the column COMMENT: nothing verifies the declaration (no IP geolocation, no KYC, no document check -- the schema has no identity fields at all), no SDN/UN/EU/UK list is consulted, and a country code cannot express region-level measures such as those applying to parts of Ukraine. Calling it screening would be exactly the kind of false statement being fixed elsewhere in this finding. DELIBERATELY_NOT_BLOCKED records RU, BY, MM, VE, CN and UA with the reason each is left out, so the omissions read as decisions rather than oversights. CONTROL GAP 2 CLOSED -- AGE. The 18+ requirement is now an explicit, recorded attestation at signup instead of a sentence nobody captured. Still a representation -- there is no age or identity verification anywhere -- and the column COMMENT says so. MIGRATION 053 APPLIED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Trial-then-rollback first (browser write surface unchanged at 143 grants both times), then applied. Verified in production: both columns present, BOTH NULLABLE BY DESIGN -- a NOT NULL with a backfill would manufacture a legal representation the user never made, which is worse than an honest NULL, so NULL can only ever mean 'row predates this column' -- shape constraint and partial index installed, and THE CONSTRAINT WAS PROVEN rather than assumed: it refused 'india', 'IND', 'i' and '12' and accepted 'IN' with age_confirmed=true. The restricted LIST is deliberately NOT encoded in a CHECK, because it is a legal input counsel must be able to change without a migration, and baking it in would make every revision a schema change and would retroactively invalidate rows recorded under a previous list. A test asserts the list is absent from the SQL. REQUIRED AT SIGNUP, OPTIONAL ON RE-ACCEPTANCE, for a reason: an existing user prompted by a version change is being asked to accept new TEXT, and re-demanding a country declaration there would either lock them out of their own account or collect a value the prompt never asked for. A restricted value is still refused if offered. VERIFICATION: 55 LEGAL-01 tests pass (up from 36), including one that recomputes the GSTIN check digit, one that cross-checks the CIN's state against the address and its ownership code against the declared company form, one that asserts no placeholder pattern survives anywhere in the rendered documents, and one that asserts the restricted-jurisdiction module still describes itself as a declaration rather than screening. `npx vite build` succeeds; eslint reports 0 errors on every touched file; the app imports with all three /api/legal routes mounted. GDPR SCOPE DECIDED AND ITS ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCES BUILT, 2026-10-23. The product owner chose to accept customers GLOBALLY INCLUDING THE EU AND UK rather than take the cheaper route of restricting signups away from those jurisdictions. That is the HARDER path, and it makes GDPR and UK GDPR apply in full rather than conditionally, so the obligations were worked through rather than noted. ARTICLE 27 APPLIES AND IS NOT EXEMPT, established rather than assumed. Article 27 obliges a controller established outside the Union to designate a representative in writing where it offers goods or services to people in the EU OR MONITORS THEIR BEHAVIOUR. BOTH LIMBS APPLY: the owner accepts EU customers, and this platform runs Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity, which is behaviour monitoring. Article 27(2)'s exemptions are narrow -- occasional processing, no large-scale special-category data, unlikely to risk rights -- and session analytics across every consenting visitor is not occasional. A SEPARATE UK REPRESENTATIVE is required on the same basis. THE REPRESENTATIVES ARE AN APPOINTMENT, NOT CODE, SO THE GAP IS MADE VISIBLE RATHER THAN OMITTED. ENTITY.euRepresentative and ENTITY.ukRepresentative render in Privacy section 1 as '[NOT YET APPOINTED - ...]' with the reason and an interim contact. Omitting the section would have read as 'not required', which is the opposite of true, and is precisely the class of misleading-by-silence this finding was opened about. A test asserts the placeholders are PRESENT while unappointed and instructs that it be inverted once they are. ARTICLE 30 RECORDS OF PROCESSING ACTIVITIES NOW EXIST: docs/legal/RECORDS_OF_PROCESSING.md. This is a hard obligation the moment EU/UK users are accepted, and it was written FROM THE CODEBASE rather than from intent -- twelve processing activities, each with its purpose, lawful basis, data categories, source table or module, recipients, retention and transfers, with file paths cited so a reviewer can verify each line. Where an earlier policy statement and the code disagreed, the code won. It also records WHAT IS NOT PROCESSED, because those absences are load-bearing: no custody of funds or assets (which is the factual basis for the PMLA position), no KYC, no Article 9 special-category data (which is the basis for the DPIA screening conclusion), no Article 22 automated decision-making with legal effect. And it records its OWN GAPS in a dedicated section -- a ROPA listing only what is in order is a sales document, and a supervisory authority reading it would find the gaps anyway. IT ALSO DECLINES TO OVERSTATE. The ROPA records that copilot conversation history is NEVER PERSISTED, because migration 018's own header documents that every copilot write sits inside a try/except that only logs. Claiming to hold conversation data that does not exist would be inaccurate in the direction that looks WORSE for us, which is still inaccurate. A test asserts this. THREE SPECIFIC GDPR SHORTFALLS IN THE PRIVACY POLICY WERE FOUND AND FIXED: (1) the response period said '30 DAYS', which is close to but not Article 12(3)'s period -- it now says WITHIN ONE MONTH and discloses the two-month extension for complex requests, since relying on an extension never disclosed is worse than not having it; (2) breach notification said only 'within the time the law requires' -- it now commits explicitly to notifying the SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY WITHIN 72 HOURS where rights are likely to be at risk, to telling the data subject directly without undue delay where the risk is HIGH, and to keeping a record of every breach whether notifiable or not; (3) Article 22 was unaddressed -- the Policy now states we do NOT make purely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect, which is worth saying on a platform where software places orders because a reader could reasonably assume otherwise. The right to object to legitimate-interest processing and the route to a named supervisory authority (the ICO for the UK) are now explicit as well. VERIFICATION: 63 LEGAL-01 tests pass, up from 55. The new ones assert the Article 27 gap is visible, the 72-hour commitment is present, the one-month period and its extension are stated, Article 22 is addressed, the ROPA exists and names every processor the Policy names, the ROPA records its own gaps and the non-processing facts, and the ROPA does not overstate the copilot. `npx vite build` succeeds; eslint 0 errors. ENGINEERING COMPLETE, 2026-10-23. The remaining 5% was three items, and one of them did not need to be asked for. SUPABASE REGION ESTABLISHED WITHOUT ASKING: ap-southeast-1 (Singapore). The ROPA recorded this as an open gap on the grounds that every reference in the repository is the placeholder your-project-ref.supabase.co -- which was true of the REPOSITORY and not of the running system. The Supavisor pooler hostname in Secrets Manager is aws-1-ap-southeast-1.pooler.supabase.com, which encodes the region directly, and the project ref lives in the DSN username. It is the SAME region the application's own compute runs in, so the database and the app are co-located and there is no additional cross-border hop between them. For an EEA/UK data subject the transfer is EEA/UK -> Singapore, with the controller in India: two third countries, no adequacy decision, which is exactly what Privacy section 7 discloses and what the processor SCCs have to cover. A ROPA that cannot say where the primary database sits is missing one of the things a ROPA exists for, so this mattered. ARTICLE 33/34 BREACH RESPONSE RUNBOOK WRITTEN: docs/legal/BREACH_RESPONSE_RUNBOOK.md. Privacy section 10 commits to 72-hour notification, and a commitment with no procedure behind it is the precise pattern this finding was opened about -- 72 hours is not long enough to invent a process in. It records that THE CLOCK STARTS ON AWARENESS rather than on completing the investigation (getting that wrong is how an organisation misses the deadline while believing it has time left), that Article 33(4) permits phased notification so a partial notice inside 72h beats a complete one after, the Article 33(3) and 34(2) content requirements, and the containment tooling THAT ALREADY EXISTS on this platform mapped to each incident type. It cites the platform's OWN incidents rather than hypotheticals: SEC-01 (three live secrets public for 70-93 days) and VAULT-01 (two customers' credentials irrecoverable because a key was lost -- recorded because IRRECOVERABLE LOSS IS A BREACH even though nobody gained access, which a runbook written only around intrusions would miss). It also records its own standing gaps, including that the unappointed Article 27 representatives BLOCK ITS OWN NOTIFICATION STEP -- there is no designated route to an EEA/UK supervisory authority today, so a notifiable breach would have to be improvised under a legal deadline. ARTICLE 35 DPIA SCREENING WRITTEN: docs/legal/DPIA_SCREENING.md. Conclusion: a full DPIA is NOT MANDATORY, with each of the three Article 35(3) triggers assessed separately rather than waved at. 35(3)(a) is not met because the automated processing evaluates MARKET DATA, not people -- there is no scoring, ranking, categorising or prediction about the user, and the decisions that affect them financially are their own instructions being executed; this is the limb where the intuitive answer on an algo-trading platform is the wrong one. 35(3)(b) is not met because FINANCIAL DATA IS NOT AN ARTICLE 9 SPECIAL CATEGORY -- a trap that would have produced a wrong mandatory-DPIA conclusion in the cautious-looking direction. 35(3)(c) is not met because a signed-in session is not a publicly accessible area. Against the authority criteria one is clearly met (systematic monitoring) and one is arguable (highly personal data), and the screening SAYS THE RESULT IS BORDERLINE RATHER THAN COMFORTABLE, recommending a focused DPIA on the session-replay processing anyway. AND THE SCREENING FOUND A REAL DEFECT, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS WORTH WRITING: MICROSOFT CLARITY WAS RECORDING AUTHENTICATED SESSIONS WITH NO MASKING. Clarity's default masking covers form inputs but NOT page text, and on a trading platform the text is the sensitive part -- account balances, position sizes, P&L, strategy logic and exchange-connection screens all render as ordinary text and would have appeared in a replay. That is an Article 5(1)(c) data-minimisation problem independent of Article 35, and it was fixable with configuration rather than legal argument. FIXED: data-clarity-mask="true" now applies to the single <main> landmark wrapping every authenticated route in App.jsx, so every signed-in page is masked BY DEFAULT rather than relying on each new page remembering. The public marketing pages render outside that element and stay unmasked, which is deliberate -- they carry no personal data and are where the analytics are actually useful. Disclosed in Privacy section 6, naming specifically what is not captured, because 'we mask sensitive data' is a claim a reader cannot check. NOT OVER-CLAIMED: the fix does not change the account-wide masking mode in the Clarity dashboard (owner-side, would be defence in depth) and does not retroactively mask recordings already captured, which should be purged on the Clarity side. Both limits are stated in the screening document. VERIFICATION: 71 LEGAL-01 tests pass, up from 63. New ones assert the runbook carries the 72-hour clock and the awareness-not-investigation rule, names the real containment tooling, cites VAULT-01 and SEC-01, and records that Article 27 blocks its own notification step; that the DPIA screening addresses all three 35(3) limbs, reaches a conclusion, calls it borderline, and does NOT claim financial data is special-category; that Clarity masking sits on the authenticated <main> landmark rather than a leaf component; that the Privacy Policy discloses the masking; and that the ROPA records the region. TWO OF MY OWN TESTS WENT STALE AND WERE CORRECTED RATHER THAN THE DOCUMENTS BENT TO FIT: one asserted the Supabase region was unknown and failed the moment it was established -- a closed gap reading as a regression -- and one broke on a markdown line wrap inside a blockquote. Both now assert content via a whitespace-squashing helper instead of raw text, so a rewrapped paragraph cannot fail a test about substance. `npx vite build` succeeds; eslint 0 errors.
findings.remaining_action: CLOSED ON THE PRODUCT OWNER'S EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION, NOT ON COUNSEL REVIEW. THIS DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ENTRY AND MUST NOT BE READ PAST. WHY THE STATUS IS ACCEPTED_NONBLOCKING AND NOT VERIFIED_FIXED: this finding's text names 'counsel-drafted ToS/Privacy/Risk-disclosure/Refund policy, versioned, with per-user acceptance recorded at the version they agreed to'. Versioned: TRUE and tested. Per-user acceptance recorded: TRUE, live in production, append-only proven by attempting UPDATE and DELETE against a real row. Counsel-drafted: FALSE. No lawyer has drafted or reviewed these documents. Marking VERIFIED_FIXED would assert in the permanent record that counsel review happened, and a false record on a legal finding is worse than an open one. WHAT THE OWNER HAS ACCEPTED, ITEMISED SO THE ACCEPTANCE IS INFORMED: (1) ARTICLE 27 REPRESENTATIVES ARE NOT APPOINTED, for either the EU or the UK. The owner has chosen to accept customers globally INCLUDING the EU and UK. Article 27 obliges a non-EU controller to designate a representative where it offers services to people in the EU OR monitors their behaviour, and BOTH limbs apply here because this platform runs Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity. THIS IS A LIVE NON-COMPLIANCE FOR THE OWNER'S OWN CHOSEN MARKET, not a drafting nicety, and it additionally blocks the breach-notification route in BREACH_RESPONSE_RUNBOOK.md section 4. It is normally bought as a service for a few hundred euros per jurisdiction per year -- the cheapest open item anywhere in this audit relative to what it closes. It renders as a VISIBLE placeholder in Privacy section 1 so a user is told rather than misled by silence, and a test asserts that placeholder stays present while unappointed. (2) PROCESSOR DPAs AND SCCs ARE NOT CONFIRMED EXECUTED with Supabase, AWS, Google, Microsoft and Sentry. Privacy section 7 states we rely on them. All five publish them and most are click-through, so this is minutes of work rather than a negotiation. findings.title: A unique index keyed on strategy_id blocks every subscriber after the first from ever deploying a marketplace listing
findings.evidence: Confirmed by reading backend_app/migrations/021_strategy_deployment_live_uniqueness.sql and backend_app/routers/library.py::deploy_marketplace_strategy together. 021 built uq_strategy_deployments_one_live, a partial UNIQUE INDEX ON strategy_deployments (strategy_id) WHERE status IN (<nine live spellings>), to stop an OWNER's own deploy call racing itself into two live rows for one strategy -- correct for a first-party deployment, where strategy_id already uniquely names the owner. deploy_marketplace_strategy writes every SUBSCRIBER's deployment row with strategy_id = owner_strategy_id (the Listing's owner strategy, shared across every subscriber, by design -- so a subscriber executes the owner's immutable version server-side rather than holding a copy of it) and user_id = the subscriber. So the first subscriber's live deployment occupied the only unique slot that strategy_id could ever grant, and every OTHER subscriber's deploy INSERT failed with 23505 unique_violation for as long as that first row stayed live -- a Listing with more than one concurrent subscriber was unusable by all but the first. Fixed exactly per this finding's first suggested remediation: new migration backend_app/migrations/044_mkt04_rekey_live_deployment_uniqueness.sql drops 021's index and recreates it as uq_strategy_deployments_one_live_per_user ON strategy_deployments (user_id, strategy_id), same nine-spelling predicate. This is a WIDER key under the identical predicate, not a different invariant: two rows that already satisfied uniqueness under the narrower (strategy_id) key necessarily still satisfy it under the wider one, so the migration is safe on existing data with no preflight duplicate check needed (021's own preflight already established there were no duplicates to begin with). Confirmed no other code path assumes global strategy_id uniqueness (grepped every .table("strategy_deployments") call site; none queries or relies on at-most-one-row-per-strategy_id across all users). Extended tests/test_strategy_lifecycle_concurrency_postgres.py (the file 021's own regression tests live in) rather than duplicating its real-PostgreSQL harness: added test_044_rekeys_to_user_and_strategy_with_the_same_predicate (static check that 044 drops the old index and recreates it on (user_id, strategy_id) naming all nine live spellings), updated _ScratchWorld's hand-built index to the new composite shape (so the harness emulates what production actually carries post-044, not 021's superseded shape), and added two new real-Postgres tests: test_mkt04_a_second_subscriber_can_deploy_while_the_first_is_still_live (two DIFFERENT user_ids, same strategy_id, both live -- the actual bug, reproduced then fixed) and test_mkt04_the_same_user_still_cannot_double_deploy_the_same_strategy (negative control: the SAME user is still refused a second live deployment of the same strategy, proving 021's original protection survives the re-key). All 12 tests in this file pass against a real local PostgreSQL 16 instance (started for this session; AERORA_TEST_DATABASE_URL, per tests/conftest.py's own naming for an explicit real-DB opt-in), including the 10 pre-existing ones (2 source-level + 8 real-Postgres, run as a clean baseline before any change, then again after). Also updated a stale docstring cross-reference to the old index name in backend_app/workers/command_worker.py. Full marketplace_pipeline / work01_command_durability / validation_sweep regression (421 tests) clean except the 2 unrelated pre-existing billing failures already confirmed earlier this session.
findings.remaining_action: CORRECTION: this entry previously said VERIFIED_FIXED with 'migration 044 must be applied to staging/production by an operator' as the only remaining step. Attempted this session: the NEW index (uq_strategy_deployments_one_live_per_user, on (user_id, strategy_id)) was successfully created in real production, but the OLD index it is supposed to replace (uq_strategy_deployments_one_live, on strategy_id alone) could NOT be dropped -- this session's Supabase MCP tooling times out on every DROP statement (see DEPLOY-04). Both unique indexes are therefore live simultaneously right now, and the OLD, narrower one still independently refuses a second marketplace subscriber's deploy with 23505 -- so MKT-04's actual defect is NOT fixed in production yet, despite the new index existing. Someone with a direct Postgres session (or the Supabase dashboard's SQL editor) needs to run `DROP INDEX uq_strategy_deployments_one_live;` to complete this.

findings.title: The market-data quality validator's default thresholds reject almost all real-shaped market data
findings.evidence: Confirmed the defect exactly as named, and traced its real blast radius: OutlierDetector._z_score_filter/_iqr_filter (reached by default -- ValidationConfig.outlier_method defaults to Z_SCORE) computed their test against the RAW price/volume LEVEL of the whole window, then rejected the ENTIRE window on a single violation. market_data_contract.quality_report, strategy_operations, strategy_service and training_worker all REUSE this exact validator per their own docstrings -- this is not dead code, it sits on real production paths. Confirmed empirically (not just by reading): a realistic trending-price + log-normal-volume series (900 bars, the platform's typical window size) was rejected by the pre-fix z-score-on-levels check on every one of several random seeds tried, while the existing test suite's own 'clean, accepted' fixture (tests/test_feed_state_and_data_quality.py's _pool()) is explicitly documented as a bounded SINE WAVE rather than anything resembling real market data, specifically to dodge this exact bug -- independent confirmation the defect is real and already known-about well enough to be worked around rather than fixed. Root cause: price and volume levels are both non-stationary (price trends/drifts, volume is approximately log-normal) by construction, so a z-score/IQR test against a non-stationary series' own mean/quantiles measures 'how far this point is from a mean the trend/burst itself moved', unrelated to whether any individual bar is actually anomalous. FIX: switched both _z_score_filter and _iqr_filter to bar-to-bar LOG-RETURNS (log(x_t/x_(t-1))) for close AND volume -- the standard transform that makes a trending/multiplicative series approximately stationary, which these tests require to mean anything. Percent-change returns were tried first and empirically still left volume's heavy right tail (ordinary volume bursts are large MULTIPLICATIVE swings) fat enough to trip the z-score on realistic data (2 violations in 30 seeds); log-returns resolved it completely (0/30). Also raised z_score_threshold 3.0->5.0 and iqr_multiplier 1.5->3.0 (both env-overridable via MARKET_DATA_Z_SCORE_THRESHOLD / MARKET_DATA_IQR_MULTIPLIER): rejecting a whole window on ANY single point beyond a per-comparison threshold has a false-positive rate that RISES WITH WINDOW SIZE regardless of what it's computed over -- for a 900-bar window, a per-point threshold calibrated for a single comparison (3 sigma / 1.5xIQR) is tripped by chance alone far more often than not; this is a general multiple-comparisons argument, not a dataset-specific calibration, and both new values were empirically verified (across 25-30 independent random seeds per method) to clear realistic trending+bursty-volume windows while STILL catching a genuine single-bar 50x price spike. Investigated the third remediation item ('make the gap threshold interval-aware') and found it already true of the current code, just not of what the ledger note assumed: GapHandler.handle's actual gap DETECTION already derives its threshold from the timeframe (`expected_diff = timedelta(minutes=_timeframe_to_minutes(timeframe)); gaps = time_diffs > expected_diff * 1.5`) -- the `max_gap_minutes` PARAMETER the caller passes in (ValidationConfig.max_gap_minutes, fixed at 5.0) is dead code, immediately overwritten by the measured gap value before it is ever read. Not a gap in this codebase's current behaviour, just an unused/confusingly-named parameter; left as-is since removing a dead parameter is outside this finding's scope and touches a shared signature. New tests/test_data02_outlier_detection_on_returns_not_levels.py (39 tests): 25 independent random seeds of realistic trending-price + bursty-volume data accepted (previously rejected); a genuine single-bar 50x spike still rejected; the existing sine-wave clean/spike fixtures still behave exactly as before (both directions, independently re-verified here); the same two properties for the non-default IQR method. Full regression: new suite + tests/test_feed_state_and_data_quality.py + tests/test_market_data_contract.py + tests/test_validation_sweep.py (542 tests) clean except pre-existing, unrelated EmptyCategoryError collection errors (confirmed pre-existing/unrelated repeatedly this session) and the 2 pre-existing billing failures already confirmed earlier this session.
findings.remaining_action: The two threshold VALUES (z_score_threshold=5.0, iqr_multiplier=3.0) are principled, empirically-verified-against-synthetic-data defaults, not a fit against this platform's own real historical return distributions -- this sandbox has no such data. The original audit's own remediation note separated 'validate on returns/log-returns' (done, this session) from 'widen or recalibrate thresholds against real historical distributions' (NOT done -- needs a session with access to real market data to fine-tune beyond the general multiple-comparisons correction applied here). Both new constants are env-overridable so this can happen without a code change.

findings.title: The training worker has no production task definition; queued training jobs stay QUEUED forever
findings.evidence: Confirmed the exact mechanism before fixing it: backend_app/backend/training_worker.py's TrainingWorker.claim_training_job performs an atomic `SET status='RUNNING' ... WHERE id = :id AND status = 'QUEUED'` transition and TrainingWorker.start()/process_iteration poll for and run such jobs -- but that module's own run_worker() docstring documents that it is deliberately never started from main.py (Requirement 16.6 / TrainingIsolator's own docstring: training must run in a separate process so a fitting job can never share the API process's interpreter, saturate Redis, or block order/execution handling), and until this fix nothing ran it as that separate process in production, so a submitted training job stayed QUEUED forever. docker-compose.yml already runs it (`python -m backend_app.backend.training_worker`, confirmed by inspection) for local dev, which is why this finding's own title specifically says 'no PRODUCTION task definition' -- the gap was in terraform/ecs.tf, not everywhere. Added a `training` entry to local.worker_definitions (terraform/ecs.tf), the same for_each-driven map that already creates both the task definition and the ECS service for backtest/dag/command/marketplace_expiry (INF-03's own fix used this same map), sized at 2 vCPU/8192 MB rather than the other four workers' 256 cpu/512 MB: core/ml_safety.py's MemoryMonitor and backend/ml_training_policy.py's own resource tiers cap an individual training run at up to 4096 MB (CAP_MAX_MEMORY), so 512 MB would not fit even one job at its own documented ceiling before counting the interpreter plus torch/tensorflow/catboost/scikit-learn already loaded. tests/test_worker_deployment_coverage.py (the existing self-enforcing guard that caught INF-03's gap the same way) could not be reused as-is: TrainingWorker is not a WorkerBase subclass, so it is invisible to that file's subclass-discovery scan, and its generic _deployed_modules() helper already counts docker-compose.yml as 'hosted' -- which would make an assertion built on it pass whether or not THIS finding ('no PRODUCTION task definition') was fixed. Added test_training_worker_is_now_hosted_ops_train_01 to that same file, asserting directly against terraform/ecs.tf's own text. Verified as a real regression test, not a tautology: git-stashed just the terraform/ecs.tf change and reran this one test, which failed with the expected message; restored the fix and reran, green. Full regression: tests/test_worker_deployment_coverage.py (7 passed, 1 xfailed -- pre-existing, unrelated ReconciliationWorker gap) + tests/test_validation_sweep.py (376 passed, 2 skipped). terraform/ecs.tf parses as valid HCL (python-hcl2; no terraform binary available in this sandbox for a real plan/validate against AWS's Fargate cpu/memory combo table, so 2048/8192 is a known-valid pair from memory, not verified against a live provider schema here).
findings.remaining_action: The terraform source now describes the production task definition and service; it has NOT been terraform apply'd (no real AWS credentials in this sandbox), so queued training jobs still stay QUEUED in production until a session with real AWS access applies this. Also unverified here: the 2048 cpu / 8192 memory Fargate combination is a textbook-valid pair from memory, not checked against a live `terraform plan`/`validate` or AWS's current Fargate task-size table, so review it on apply. Separately, no alerting exists yet for a training job stuck QUEUED beyond some bound even once the worker is running (e.g. the worker crashes and ECS keeps restarting it into a bad state) -- out of scope for this pass, which only closes the 'nothing runs this process' gap the title names. CONFIRMED still true with real AWS access this session: `ecs ListServices` on the real `vyomquant-cluster` (ap-southeast-1, live scoped CI credential) returns only vyomquant-api-service-cjema2sl -- no training worker service exists, so queued training jobs are still permanently stuck QUEUED in production today. UPDATE same session: terraform 1.9.8 now installed in this sandbox; `terraform validate` passes for this worker's task definition (2048 cpu / 8192 memory) against the real AWS provider schema -- the Fargate size pair is schema-valid, though AWS's own Fargate-combo acceptance is still only checked at apply time, not by validate. Remains EXTERNAL_BLOCKED on the state backend: s3://vyomquant-terraform-state does not exist yet (NoSuchBucket), so `terraform apply` is not runnable from here until that bucket + lock table are bootstrapped. Creating the service directly via raw `ecs register-task-definition`/`create-service` was considered and deliberately not done this pass (same reasoning as INF-03: would diverge real infra from terraform source without a plan, and is a production-infrastructure-creation action needing explicit human confirmation first).
