findings.title: A caller could set capital/trade_size_pct/stop_loss_pct/max_drawdown_pct on deploy and have it silently dropped -- the live deploy path had no equivalent of the deleted route's refusal
findings.evidence: Found while root-causing a real CI failure (job 117485524636, tests/test_deploy_strategy_accepts_only_what_it_applies.py, AttributeError: module 'strategy_operations' has no attribute 'deploy_strategy') -- not from a targeted security review, but it surfaced a real gap once traced. `strategy_operations.deploy_strategy` was correctly deleted by an earlier session's API-01 (commit 396d210) as a permanently shadowed duplicate route (routers/strategies.py was mounted first and always won the same path, so it had been dead code since the day both were added). That deletion was correct. But tracing the real, reachable deploy path -- routers.strategies.deploy_bot / resume_strategy -> _deploy_current_version_paper -> StrategyService.deploy_version -- found that `assert_deploy_params_applicable` (the refusal the dead route used to run) never travelled to the replacement. `deploy_version`'s own request model (DeploymentBindingRequest) has no field for capital/trade_size_pct/stop_loss_pct/max_drawdown_pct at all, and deploy_bot's raw request body dict was never read for them either. A caller setting a stop-loss on deploy got a 200 and had it silently dropped -- a trader who believes they set a 2% stop and gets a bot running with none, exactly the scenario assert_deploy_params_applicable exists to prevent, just one layer removed from the route this had been pinned against. assert_blueprint_startable (the deploy_strategy's OTHER protection, against deploying a blueprint that cannot start a bot) needed no equivalent fix: deploy_version already calls it directly (strategy_service.py:1858) and maps its failure through DeployRejected(http_status=422), which _deploy_current_version_paper already handles -- that protection travelled to the live route correctly. Fixed by calling assert_deploy_params_applicable in _deploy_current_version_paper before anything else runs (same ordering the deleted route used) and having deploy_bot forward its request body to it. resume_strategy's own route takes no body, so there is nothing for it to forward -- the gap only ever existed on the deploy path, not resume.
findings.verification_level: root-caused against a real GitHub Actions failure; verified by direct behavioral calls to the live route function (not source inspection), mocking only get_strategy_service: a supplied risk/capital parameter is refused with 422 before the service is ever reached, a zero value counts as supplied, omitting the parameters reaches the real service call unaffected
findings.remaining_action: Get this merged and confirm on the next real CI run that test_deploy_strategy_accepts_only_what_it_applies.py's full 27 tests pass. Not yet exercised against a real deployed backend (e.g. a live POST /api/strategies/{id}/deploy with a stop_loss_pct set) -- the fix is verified at the function level, not end-to-end through a running server.

findings.title: RedactingLogFilter destroyed a lazy %-format placeholder in a denied-key-shaped label, crashing the kill-switch's 'audit write failed, never raise' fallback and turning a successful halt into a false 500
findings.evidence: Found root-causing a real CI failure (tests/test_role_granularity_and_audit.py::TestHighBlastRadiusEndpoints::test_kill_switch_succeeds_for_operator_with_valid_reason, assert 500 == 200) by reproducing the real exception with a full traceback rather than assuming the test was stale. The 500's message was 'Kill switch error: not all arguments converted during string formatting' -- a classic %-format arg-count mismatch, not the DB error it looked like at first. Traced it to core/observability.py's RedactingLogFilter, attached to every root logging handler by install_root_log_redaction() (LOG-01) and therefore reached by every logger in the process, SafetyAudit included. _redact_key_values_in_text() runs against record.msg BEFORE Python's lazy %-logging substitutes record.args into it, so for a %-style call it sees the literal, unsubstituted template text, placeholders and all. core/safety_audit.py:record_safety_transition()'s own 'audit write failed, log the record for recovery' critical call logs '...authorization_source=%s reason=%r detail=%s'. 'authorization_source' matches the deny-list's 'authorization' entry (SECRET_KEY_NAMES) as a contiguous token subsequence, so the filter treated the literal text '%s' immediately after 'authorization_source=' as the value to redact and replaced it with '[redacted]' -- deleting one of the format string's 11 conversion specifiers while record.args (redacted separately, per item, never shortened) stayed at 11 elements. record.getMessage()'s msg %% self.args then raised TypeError the instant any handler tried to render the line. This is exactly the failure mode core/safety_audit.py's module docstring says record_safety_transition() exists to prevent: 'A safety control must not fail to engage because its audit row could not be written... never raises into the caller.' The kill switch HAD already engaged by this point (GlobalKillSwitch.activate()'s local latch is set before the DB write is attempted) -- the crash was purely in the best-effort logging fallback for a failed audit write, but because routers/admin.py:global_kill_switch() wraps the whole body in a bare 'except Exception: raise HTTPException(500, ...)', that logging crash propagated all the way out as a 500 telling the operator the halt failed, when it had actually succeeded. The DB write itself failed in this test only because the SQLite test-lane fallback has no safety_control_audit table (it is accessed via raw SQL, not an ORM model, so the sqlite-lane Base.metadata.create_all() bootstrap fixture never creates it) -- but the SAME crash would hit a real production DB outage during a real kill-switch activation, which is precisely the scenario the 'never raises' contract is written for.
findings.verification_level: root-caused with a real, unmodified traceback captured by temporarily logging traceback.format_exc() in the route's except block (removed before commit), then confirmed character-for-character via a standalone script that the unpatched redact_text() deletes the %s after 'authorization_source=' (11 specifiers -> 10) while the patched version preserves the template exactly (11 -> 11) and still redacts a real literal secret value. Full test suite re-run after the fix: tests/test_role_granularity_and_audit.py 11/11 (was 10/11), tests/test_log01_root_redaction_covers_every_logger.py, tests/test_log_redaction.py (370 tests total, all passing before and after except one pre-existing, unrelated failure in test_exchange_credential_log_redaction.py -- confirmed via git stash to fail identically with and without this change), tests/test_trade02_kill_switch_fails_closed.py, tests/test_kill03_authoritative_global_halt.py.
findings.remaining_action: Not yet exercised against a real deployed backend with a real database outage induced during a live kill-switch activation -- the fix is verified at the function level (redact_text() preserves %-format templates) and via the existing test suite, not end-to-end against production infrastructure. Separately, the SQLite test lane still has no safety_control_audit table at all (it is raw-SQL-only, no ORM model), so this unit test only exercises the 'DB write fails' branch by accident of the test lane's schema gap rather than by deliberate fault injection -- worth a dedicated test that injects a DB failure on purpose, but out of scope for this fix.

findings.title: GET /api/strategies/{id} lost its 200/minute rate limit when API-01 deleted the shadowed duplicate that carried it
findings.evidence: Found root-causing a real CI failure (tests/test_task_8_2_deploy_preflight.py::TestTheRouteIsReachableAndNotShadowed::test_the_limit_matches_the_comparable_existing_get, ValueError: substring not found) rather than assuming the test was stale. That test reads strategy_operations.py's source for '@router.get("/strategies/{strategy_id}")' to find the rate limit preflight_deploy_version is deliberately kept matching under Requirement 22.2 ('the same get action on the closest equivalent resource'). That literal decorator no longer exists in that file -- confirmed via 'git log -S' that API-01 (commit 396d210, the same commit that caused DEPLOY-03) deleted it as one of eleven permanently shadowed duplicate route handlers, correctly, since routers/strategies.py's own `@router.get("/{strategy_id}")` is mounted first and always won the identical path. The deleted copy carried `@limiter.limit("200/minute")`; the live route in strategies.py never did. Confirmed via `backend_app/core/rate_limit.py`'s own `Limiter(...)` construction (no `default_limits` argument) that slowapi applies NO blanket rate limit to an undecorated route, so this was a real, unmitigated gap: GET /api/strategies/{id} could be called at unlimited rate, where every comparable strategy-detail GET in this router (and the dead duplicate it replaced) carries 200/minute.
findings.verification_level: Added @limiter.limit("200/minute") to strategies.py's get_strategy_route (matching the exact value the deleted duplicate carried and what preflight_deploy_version already expects to match), and pointed the test's comparable-route lookup at strategies.py, where that route now lives. Verified via tests/test_task_8_2_deploy_preflight.py (42/42, was 41/42), tests/test_api01_no_shadowed_routes.py, tests/test_subscriber_restricted_operations.py, tests/test_task_4_3_deploy_prerequisite_gate.py (296 tests total, no regressions), and a smoke test against the real backend_app.main.app confirming GET /api/strategies/{id} still resolves (401 without auth, not 404/500).
findings.remaining_action: Not yet exercised against a real deployed backend by actually sending 201+ requests in a minute and observing a 429 -- the fix is verified at the decorator/source level (the limiter is present and set to the intended value) and via the existing test suite, not by driving the real limit end-to-end. Worth checking whether any OTHER route API-01 deleted as a shadowed duplicate also carried a rate limiter, auth dependency, or other protection that did not travel to its live replacement -- this is the second of eleven deletions found to have a gap (after DEPLOY-03's parameter-refusal gap); the remaining nine have not been individually re-audited for the same pattern.

findings.title: Global redaction filter corrupted its own REDACTED placeholder when a caller's log line already contained one, turning '[REDACTED]' into '[REDACTED]]]'
findings.evidence: Surfaced only after PR #32's own sandbox=False fix let tests/test_exchange_credential_log_redaction.py reach further than it ever had before, exposing a second, previously-unreachable bug behind the first: the regex-driven key=value redaction in backend_app/core/observability.py's _redact_key_values_in_text ran again on a value that a caller (or an earlier filter pass -- install_root_log_redaction() attaches a filter to every root handler at import time, a process-global side effect once any test imports main.py) had already replaced with REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER, re-matching the placeholder text itself as a 'key=value' pair and wrapping it a second time. Reproduced deterministically by running tests/test_log01_root_redaction_covers_every_logger.py (which imports main.py, installing the global filter) before the exchange-credential test in the same pytest process -- that ordering reliably produced the exact corruption; the exchange-credential test alone never hit it.
findings.verification_level: Added _ALREADY_REDACTED_RE, matching the skip idiom LOG-02's _BARE_PERCENT_SPEC_RE already established in the same function (treat the match like a non-denied key, skip past it rather than redact again). Verified via tests/test_exchange_credential_log_redaction.py, tests/test_log01_root_redaction_covers_every_logger.py, LOG-02's own regression test, and the two files run together in the exact order that reproduced the bug.

findings.title: ConnectionSharder.get_shard_for_user used Python's per-process-randomized hash(), breaking its own 'a user always connects to the same shard' guarantee across worker processes
findings.evidence: Surfaced as the first red 01 PR Check on main since DEPLOY-02's fix landed -- a push carrying only ledger JSON/CSV changes (commit 2f63af6, PR #43) could not have caused a real regression, so the failure was investigated rather than assumed to be unrelated noise. tests/test_websocket_cluster.py::test_shard_distribution failed with 'Shard 0 has 197 users, expected ~250' (tolerance +/-20% of 250, i.e. 200-300). Root-caused to backend_app/backend/websocket_cluster.py::ConnectionSharder.get_shard_for_user calling Python's built-in hash() on the user_id string -- CPython randomizes string hashing per process via PYTHONHASHSEED (on by default since 3.3, to resist hash-flooding DoS), so the exact same 1000 deterministic user_ids land in different shards on every process start; this run's seed happened to skew shard 0 outside tolerance. This is not merely a flaky test: the method's own docstring promises 'a user always connects to the same shard', which is false across any two processes with different hash seeds -- i.e. any two gunicorn workers in a real deployment. Confirmed ConnectionSharder has no other call site anywhere in backend_app/ (grepped the whole tree), so nothing live is currently mis-routed -- same 'built, tested, never wired in' pattern this ledger documents elsewhere (RT-11, HY-02) -- but the class exists and is tested as working correctness, not test-only scaffolding, so the gap is real for whenever it is wired in.
findings.verification_level: Fixed by hashing with hashlib.sha256 instead of hash() -- stable across processes and interpreter restarts. Verified directly: the same two user_ids resolve to the same shard under PYTHONHASHSEED=1/2/3 after the fix (varied before it), and tests/test_websocket_cluster.py passes 12/12 under five different hash seeds (0-4), where it was previously seed-dependent.

findings.title: Migrations 019 through 046 (14 files, 10 new tables) were never applied to the real production database -- despite application code, tests and several ledger entries assuming they were live
findings.evidence: Discovered while verifying TENANT-01's production wiring: OrderWatchdog was crashing every ~30s in the real ECS task's logs with `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column execution_records.venue_order_id does not exist` -- the exact column migration 030 adds. Rather than fixing 030 alone, ran the schema-contract parser (scripts/migration_preflight.py's expectations_for_file, reused for 019-047) against the real production Supabase project (wrkexcjqnidkdrayhlsi) via the Supabase MCP server's execute_sql (direct psycopg2 was blocked by this sandbox's network policy; execute_sql goes over Supabase's management API instead). Result: of 019-047, only 020, 021, 022 and 047 (role/grants only, applied by a prior session) were live. NOT-APPLIED: 019 (training governance columns + training_governance_decisions), 024 (referral commission duplicate guard), 025 (bot_ownership_claims -- WORK-03's cross-process single-owner lock), 026 (fee_records RLS), 027 (referral ledger currency column), 028 (safety_control_audit -- the kill switch's durable audit trail), 029 (referral_obligations), 030 (execution_records.venue_order_id), 032 (referral_payouts terminal-evidence constraint), 034+038 (strategy_deployments browser-role guard trigger -- SEC-16's actual DB-level control), 036 (order_audit_log), 037 (profiles billing columns), 039 (market_data_source_measurements), 040 (trade_history), 044 (the MKT-04 re-keyed unique index), 045 (webhook_events -- SEC-03's durable idempotency store), 046 (signal_audit_log). findings.title: process_referral_commission's installed signature does not match what backend_app/routers/billing.py calls it with, so every Stripe referral commission RPC call has been failing silently
findings.evidence: Found while adapting migration 024 (MONEY-01's double-commission race fix) to the real production schema. The real installed function's signature, read directly off pg_proc, is process_referral_commission(p_payment_id varchar, p_referred_user_id uuid, p_subscription_tier varchar, p_payment_amount_usd numeric) -- note the second parameter is named p_referred_user_id. backend_app/routers/billing.py:2757-2764 calls it via supabase-py's .rpc('process_referral_commission', {...}) with the key 'p_referred_id' (not 'p_referred_user_id'). PostgREST resolves a dict-based .rpc() call by parameter NAME, so this mismatch means the call could never resolve to the installed function -- PostgREST would answer 'function not found', caught by billing.py's bare except and logged as an error, never raised. Zero 'Referral commission processed' log lines appear anywhere in 7 days of production logs (checked directly), consistent with every Stripe referral-commission credit having silently failed for at least that long. FIXED TWO WAYS, NEITHER REQUIRING A DROP (which this session's tooling could not execute -- see DEPLOY-04): (1) backend_app/routers/billing.py's RPC call was changed to pass 'p_referred_user_id' (the real, installed parameter name) instead of 'p_referred_id'. (2) The function's BODY (not its signature/parameter names, which CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cannot change without DROP FUNCTION first) was replaced via CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION to add the atomic MONEY-01 guard: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (payment_id) WHERE payment_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING, with the referral_wallets upsert made conditional on the insert having actually happened, using the REAL wallet columns (balance_usd, total_earned_usd -- confirmed via information_schema, NOT migration 024's assumed pending_balance_usd/lifetime_earnings_usd) and preserving the installed version's referral_relationships.status='active' filter that 024's own replacement would have silently dropped. Also added: uq_referral_commission_payment (partial unique index on payment_id) and locked EXECUTE down to service_role only (REVOKE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated), matching 024's original intent. TRACEABILITY CORRECTION (this session): fix_commit was the untraceable placeholder 'PENDING_COMMIT', which made this entry's claim unverifiable against the repository -- acceptance criterion 12 asks that the branch and commit contain the exact changes validated. Resolved to 38d23ee8, 3ec8115f by searching `git log --all --grep` for this finding's own id and confirming each hash is an ancestor of main with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. No code, status, severity or evidence claim was changed by this correction.
findings.verification_level: production; function body, grants and the new unique index confirmed via pg_proc/pg_indexes/has_function_privilege after applying. The application-code fix (billing.py) is not yet exercised against a real Stripe webhook in this session.
findings.remaining_action: Not verified end-to-end against a real Stripe checkout.session.completed webhook for a referred user (would require either waiting for real traffic or a test-mode Stripe event). The installed function's parameter name (p_referred_user_id) could not be renamed to match billing.py's original call (p_referred_id) because PostgreSQL refuses a parameter rename via CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION without DROP FUNCTION first, which this session's Supabase MCP tooling could not execute -- so the fix went the other direction (fixed the caller, not the callee's name). If a future session can run DROP FUNCTION directly (e.g. via the Supabase dashboard's SQL editor), renaming the DB parameter to match 024's original intent and reverting billing.py's key name would be a pure cleanup, not a behavior change.

findings.title: 35 PostgreSQL-gated test files are named in no PostgreSQL lane, so 432 tests -- including a P0's own regression suite -- skip in every lane and assert nothing against a real server
findings.evidence: Found while checking CI-06's own open question against real GitHub Actions data. Both PostgreSQL jobs in 01-pr-check.yml name the files they run EXPLICITLY; neither runs `pytest tests/`. A file that gates itself on AERORA_TEST_DATABASE_URL and is named in neither list therefore runs against a real server NOWHERE, while still looking accounted for: the unit-tests lane has no DATABASE_URL by design so the file SKIPS there, and a skip is not a failure, so a fully green run reports nothing wrong. MEASURED against the real job logs of run 39695784610 (head dfd9ca24, all 8 jobs green): 49 test files gate on that variable; the database-tests lane ran 4 of them (26 tests) and the provisioning lane 13 (262 tests), 11 of which are in the gated set; the remaining 35 files contributed 432 SKIPPED results to that run's '790 skipped' and not one assertion against PostgreSQL. 472 tests are defined across those 35 files. They are not peripheral: they include test_sec07_profiles_platform_columns_postgres.py (the regression suite for SEC-07, a P0), the cross-tenant isolation matrix, fee_records RLS, tenant_db_context, the paper-trading ledger/unfunded-order/service-role-only/fill-atomicity suites, concurrent exposure, stale-execution recovery, referral-commission idempotence and single-currency enforcement, payout atomicity, WORK-03's cross-process single-owner bot lock, KILL-03's durable audit trail (its 6 realaudit tests were exactly 6 of the skips) and RT-16's watchdog adjudication. Each asserts an RLS, privilege, trigger, constraint or transaction-isolation guarantee SQLite cannot express, which is why each file gates itself rather than asserting something weaker. FIX (commit 08123b86): a new step in the provisioning-and-isolation job -- the one that has already provisioned the full schema from repository source twice and so has the anon/authenticated/service_role substrate these tests need -- runs all 35, as a separate step so a failure is attributable, with no continue-on-error. New guard tests/test_every_postgres_gated_file_runs_in_a_postgres_lane.py parses the workflow and fails if a PostgreSQL-gated file is named in no PostgreSQL lane; its 5 tests include a negative control on its own detector and a staleness check on its (explicitly reasoned) exemption list. The detector strips comment lines first -- without that, merely DISCUSSING a file in a comment inside a PostgreSQL job marks it covered, which it did to itself on the first run. RESULT, first execution against real PostgreSQL 17 (run 39728990457, job 119660118669): 625 passed, 11 skipped, 1 failed in 41.88s. The single failure was a genuine finding the lane existed to surface -- a stale strict xfail in test_p10d_referral_settlement_lifecycle_postgres.py whose 'migration 032 is NOT APPLIED' premise the provisioning log disproves; fixed in de87b620. The 11 skips are PAPER-05's 10 (see that entry -- not root-caused) and one opt-in DSN-file check. Negative control for the guard, run against the workflow text read from `git show HEAD:...` with the working tree untouched: exactly 35 uncovered at HEAD, 0 after the change. CLOSED: PR #52 merged to main as 611708c2, and the post-merge 01-pr-check.yml run 39731822360 on that exact commit is green on ALL 8 jobs. The new step -- 'Run every remaining PostgreSQL-gated test file' inside Provisioning, Privilege Hardening & Tenant Isolation -- reports 626 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed in 42.38s against the postgres:17-alpine service, with the job's other steps unchanged (233 passed, 7 skipped for the original lane; 22 passed, 13 deselected for the production verifiers) and scripts/verify_schema_drift.py still reporting RESULT: NO DRIFT. So 432 tests that asserted nothing against a real server in run 39695784610 now assert against one, and the two guards added with the fix hold on main.
findings.verification_level: code+test; verified on main in GitHub Actions against real PostgreSQL 17
findings.remaining_action: None for CI-11 itself: the gap is closed, the guard prevents it reopening, and the lane is green on main (611708c2). TWO RESIDUALS, both recorded rather than closed, neither caused by this change: (1) PAPER-05's 10 atomicity tests still SKIP inside the new step, for a reason that contradicts the same job's own provisioning log -- tracked under PAPER-05, needs a live PostgreSQL session to diagnose, and the lane now provides one. (2) Five files are deliberately EXEMPT from the guard with stated reasons (the conftest gate itself, the Redis-gated webhook delivery test, the two whose subject is the workflow YAML or the SQLite lane, and the guard itself) -- each is a judgement call a reviewer should check rather than take on trust. SCOPE NOTE, to prevent this entry being over-read: it proves that a database provisioned from REPOSITORY SOURCE satisfies these RLS, privilege, trigger, constraint and isolation invariants. It asserts nothing about the production database, whose migration state is DEPLOY-04's subject.

findings.title: A module-level PostgreSQL gate placed below six database-independent tests discarded them in every lane, so AUD-01's signal-audit writers had no running test while the suite looked green
findings.evidence: tests/test_aud01_signal_audit_log.py defines nine tests. Collection reported '0 items / 1 skipped'. Six of the nine are the fake-PostgREST unit tests the module's own docstring describes as proving 'every writer calls it correctly and that a failure to record the audit row never breaks the write it is recording'; they need no database. They sit ABOVE a module-level pytest.skip(..., allow_module_level=True) (itself preceded by a module-level pytest.importorskip('psycopg2')), and both forms abort collection of the WHOLE file, so those six went with it. They therefore ran in NO lane and nothing reported it: neither PostgreSQL job lists this file so the gate never opened, and the SQLite lane skipped the module BEFORE collecting them, so they never appeared even as a skip. Confirmed against the real log of run 39695784610: this file contributes no line at all to that run's 14,652 passed / 790 skipped. FIX (d95c8c7f): scoped the gate to the class that needs it, following this suite's own existing convention -- tests/test_production_security_probe_rolls_back_postgres.py already gates per-test with a pytest.mark.skipif named _needs_pg, which is exactly why its six source-inspection tests DO run in the SQLite lane -- and moved the psycopg2 import into the db fixture so a missing driver cannot delete database-independent tests either. Collection went from 0 items to 9: 6 passed, 3 correctly skipped without a database. The six PASS, so the writer logic was already correct; it simply was not being checked. The same lazy-import change was applied to the probe file: its six tests were NOT actively lost (psycopg2 is a declared dependency so its importorskip never fires in CI, and the real log shows them passing) but the structure carried the identical latent failure mode. NEW GUARD tests/test_module_level_gates_discard_no_tests.py fails if any module places a collection-aborting gate below tests defined above it, with a negative control (the detector must flag the pre-fix shape) and a positive control (a gate above every test is correct and must not be flagged). NEGATIVE CONTROL run against the original file text read from `git show HEAD:<path>` with the working tree untouched: the detector reports gate line 212 and names all six discarded AUD-01 tests, and gate line 262 with six for the probe file, and reports nothing for either post-fix version. Regression slice -k 'aud01 or aud02 or signal_audit or audit_trail or module_level_gates or security_probe': 53 passed, 25 skipped, 0 failed. Test-only change; no production code touched.
findings.verification_level: code+test (verified locally this session, with negative control)
findings.remaining_action: None for the defect itself. The file's three real-PostgreSQL migration tests still need a server; they are wired into the provisioning lane under CI-11 and pass there (run 39728990457). Only two modules in the suite had this shape and both are fixed, so the guard currently protects an already-clean tree.
